#2087. Un Kevin De Bruyne così a Napoli non s’è mai visto. Colpa sua o di chi lo allena?

Quindi Kevin De Bruyne può ancora giocare così. Come quando illuminava il Manchester City, come stasera a Bruxelles, dove è stato il centro di gravità permanente del Belgio di Mark Van Bommel, che ha schiantato l’Italia di Roberto Mancini. Non ha segnato, ma è entrato in tutte le azioni dei gol belgi, ha confermato di essere ancora oggi un grande giocatore.

Un campione, inserito in un contesto che gli gira attorno. È questo che in azzurro non hanno mai visto, da quando KdB è arrivato alla corte di De Laurentiis. Le statistiche individuali sono sempre state buone, perfino ottime, ma Kevin non è mai diventato l’uomo al centro del Napoli. È qualcosa in più, a volte estraneo rispetto alla squadra. Basti pensare che, nello snocciolare la formazione tipo, alla fine nessuno sa davvero dove inserirlo. Perché non si è inserito, anche se poi, quando è in campo, è lui a mandare regolarmente in porta i giocatori. Capita nei migliori matrimoni, anche calcistici: persino il miglior giocatore al mondo - e non stiamo dicendo che De Bruyne lo sia - può non essere funzionale al contesto in cui si ritrova.

Partiamo dalla seconda parte della domanda: a Napoli l’hanno allenato Antonio Conte e Massimiliano Allegri. La crisi di rigetto con il primo è stata, oseremmo dire, fisiologica: disciplinato sì, soldatino no, non è un giocatore da Conte. Per Max, però, sembrava perfetto: esperto e di qualità. E invece non sta funzionando. Al netto delle difficoltà incontrate da Allegri negli ultimi tempi, resta il dubbio che non sia (anche? Solo?) colpa del giocatore. Le recenti dichiarazioni della sua compagna vanno in questa direzione, peraltro. La sensazione è che, volente o nolente, De Bruyne a Napoli non si sia ambientato, e che questo discorso valga a 360°. Resta qualche mese - fino a gennaio, o magari a giugno - per cercare di non rendere una grande operazione di mercato un flop di campo. Visto il KdB di Bruxelles, sarebbe davvero un peccato.

#2085. West Ham should be keeping tabs on situation of out-of-favour Leeds United striker: Opinion

West Ham have a chance to propel themselves into title-winning contention in the January transfer window. WHU have been impressive to start the year and are the clear top scorers in the Championship, despite struggling to nail down a number nine.

West Ham United should be looking at Mateo Joseph as a potential January addition, with the Leeds United forward offering an interesting opportunity for Scott Parker as he looks to guide the Hammers back into the Premier League.

Parker has inherited a side with plenty of attacking quality, but the centre-forward position remains an area that could benefit from strengthening. With Joseph looking to be available in January, West Ham must be paying attention to his situation.

Joel Piroe has scored around four league goals since arriving on loan from Leeds, while Taty Castellanos has struggled to establish himself as a consistent goalscoring threat. West Ham are scoring freely, with 37 goals in their opening 15 Championship fixtures, but another option could prove important during the second half of the campaign.

Joseph would offer something different. The 23-year-old spent last season on loan at Mallorca, making 29 La Liga appearances, including 19 starts.

He registered two goals and three assists, with his underlying numbers suggesting there could be more to come from him in front of goal. His 4.92 expected goals compared with two actual strikes indicates that his finishing did not necessarily reflect the opportunities he found, according to FotMob.

Versatility is another attraction. Primarily a centre-forward or right winger, Joseph can operate across the frontline, giving Parker additional tactical flexibility. He also has experience of winning promotion from the Championship, having featured 39 times for Leeds during their successful 2024/25 campaign, recording three goals and three assists.

There is, however, an obvious complication. Joseph suffered an ACL injury while at Mallorca in April and has been recovering at Leeds. He is targeting a return to competitive action around January or February 2027, meaning any potential move would carry considerable fitness risk.

His modest senior goalscoring record also means West Ham would be taking a chance rather than signing an established Championship marksman. Nevertheless, that could make him an attainable target. Leeds are reportedly open to moving him on, while his injury situation could create an opportunity for a loan agreement with a potential obligation to buy.

West Ham need to be careful with their January recruitment, particularly with promotion within reach. However, Joseph’s age, versatility and previous Championship experience make him an intriguing option. If his recovery progresses as hoped, he could provide valuable competition for Piroe without requiring a significant initial investment.

#2084. Italia, Donnarumma: "Alti e bassi che fanno parte del percorso, siamo arrivati un po' stanchi"

Il capitano dell'Italia Gianluigi Donnarumma, ai microfoni della Rai, ha parlato così dopo la sconfitta contro il Belgio. "Purtroppo fa parte del percorso, abbiamo iniziato un nuovo percorso e questi alti e bassi possono capitare. E' stata una partita splendida con la Francia, siamo arrivati un po' stanchi. Non eravamo dei fenomeni prima, non siamo scarsi ora. Nessuno si aspettava questo percorso interessante in Nations League facendo ottime partite, il Belgio però è stato superiore e dobbiamo migliorare".

Quanto è importante prendere una sconfitta non all'italiana? "La cosa che ci deve far riflettere è che abbiamo preso troppi contropiedi, bisognava fare delle preventive in più. Questa sconfitta ci può e ci deve servire, il mister lo ha già detto che bisogna rialzare la testa. Stasera ha fatto male, ci tenevamo tutti ad andare avanti".

Non c'è stata una reazione dopo i tre gol del Belgio, ha inciso la partita con la Francia? "Si, quando giochi una partita così intensa ed entusiasmante come quella di San Siro rigiocare dopo due giorni non è facile. Non deve essere una scusa, sicuramente ha fatto sì che eravamo meno brillanti. Fa parte della crescita e bisogna non ripetere più questi errori".

Tanti cambi per questa Nazionale, dovrete aiutare Mancini in questo con i nuovi. "Il mister è speciale, può dare una mano importante. Noi dobbiamo dare una mano ai giovani, non c'è tanto tempo perché ci giochiamo le qualificazioni all'Europeo ma devono giocare di più e fare esperienza. Ci sono giovani interessanti che ci possono dare una mano, devono andare forte e giocare di più".

#2083. Southampton loanee has chance to kickstart his spell after Keven Schlotterbeck injury: Opinion

Southampton had a mixed summer transfer window but one major blow was the sale of Taylor Harwood-Bellis. The Saints brought in multiple defenders in a bid to replace him and one of which was Zach Abbott who joined on loan.

Abbott has a chance to change the course of his Southampton loan spell following Keven Schlotterbeck’s shoulder injury. The Nottingham Forest youngster was introduced during the 1-0 defeat at Preston North End and delivered a composed performance across 79 minutes at centre-back, earning a 6.8 FotMob rating.

It was only his second Championship appearance since arriving on loan in September, but the circumstances have created an opportunity he desperately needs. At 20, Abbott is still developing, and regular first-team football was the obvious attraction of his temporary move to St Mary’s.

Abbott has been honest about his frustration at the lack of minutes, admitting to BBC Radio Solent that he has been “itching for a lot more”. His response to limited opportunities has been to remain patient, work hard in training and take advice from his experienced teammates.

The numbers underline how little football Abbott has played. He has accumulated just 124 Championship minutes across two appearances, completing 74 of his 84 passes at an impressive 88.1% accuracy. He has also won two of his three aerial duels, with his success rate ranking in the 86th percentile among full-backs.

Although the sample size is small, his Preston performance offered encouragement that he can handle the demands of Championship football. His versatility is another advantage, having previously demonstrated an ability to operate at both centre-back and right-back.

Southampton are 7th after 15 games, with 24 points, and remain firmly in the promotion conversation. However, Schlotterbeck’s expected six-week absence leaves Tonda Eckert needing to find a reliable defensive replacement. Nathan Wood and Jack Stephens provide competition, but Abbott has already shown he can step in without looking out of place.

This is an important period for Abbott and both clubs. He joined Southampton to gain the senior experience that was difficult to secure at Nottingham Forest, but his lack of involvement has reportedly raised the possibility of a January recall.

A sustained run of appearances before the new year would change that picture considerably. It would provide Forest with the Championship experience they wanted him to gain and give Southampton another capable defensive option during a crucial period of their campaign.

The upcoming home fixture against Derby County after the international break could be particularly important. Abbott has already reached an FA Cup semi-final and featured in the Europa League, so his potential is clear.

Now he needs regular opportunities to demonstrate it at Championship level. Schlotterbeck’s injury is unfortunate, but it could be the opening Abbott has been waiting for. Southampton should give him the chance to make the most of it.

#2081. Mancini sbaglia partita, De Bruyne fa a pezzi l’Italia. A Napoli è colpa di Allegri? Milan, ecco Krosche che vuole lo scudetto con Tresoldi e Inacio. Tre giovani per Napoli: Varela, Bakola e Cacciamani. Juve punta Sorloth e Balde

Pesante ritorno sulla terra per l’Italia che soffre il Belgio come e più di quanto successo nella gara d’andata. Una disfatta difficile da accettare dopo la partita perfetta contro la Francia, ma facile da spiegare. Il Belgio è più forte di noi e si sapeva, il dominio è stato totale. E’ il loro gioco ad alta velocità con grande tecnica che ci mette in crisi, il movimento frenetico, le rotazioni con cambi di posizione, gli esterni che spingono, senza un centravanti vero, il pressing costante, gli azzurri non c'hanno capito niente, non hanno mai trovato gli avversari perdendo le posizioni e tutti i duelli. Una sconfitta che è pure figlia di alcune scelte di Mancini difficilmente comprensibili come Pisilli centrocampista messo a presidiare la zona destra, o il lento Fagioli opposto a giocatori molto veloci, non era la sua partita. Nel primo tempo gli azzurri non l’hanno mai vista. Ma anche Koleosho è andato in difficoltà nella fase difensiva. Una sconfitta che però non può spazzare via tutto quello che di buono s’è visto in questo Mancini-bis, con la consapevolezza che la strada sarà ancora lunga prima di trovare equilibrio e personalità compiute. Mancini che, fra l’altro, potrebbe tornare in discussione se Malagò dovesse perdere le elezioni del quattordici dicembre, ributtando tutto nel caos. Speriamo di no.

In attesa, dobbiamo sottolineare l’ennesima grande partita di De Bruyne, assoluto dominatore di tutte le partite della sua nazionale. E allora come si spiegano le sue prestazioni insufficienti e le sue difficoltà a prendere in mano il Napoli?

E’ molto probabile che il belga non gradisca il tipo di calcio passivo proposto da Allegri, soffra il grande lavoro che gli viene chiesto nella fase difensiva. La squadra non gli gira attorno, non si diverte e così perde gran parte della sua enorme qualità e il sorriso. Una riflessione andrebbe fatta, anche se alla fine è probabile che il giocatore finisca al Psv Eindhoven già a gennaio facendo risparmiare sei milioni netti alle casse del Napoli. Sarebbe una sconfitta per tutti non essere riusciti a godere del suo enorme talento. Ma del Napoli riparleremo più avanti.

Dopo la nazionale, riecco il campionato con tutte le problematiche e il mercato di gennaio alla porta. La grande svolta probabilmente arriverà da Cardinale che s’è messo in testa di vincere lo scudetto, quindi ha pronti gli acquisti per sistemare i punti deboli del Milan. Il budget c’è, il nuovo capo dell’area tecnica pure. Come sappiamo, anche se arriverà ufficialmente solo a gennaio, è già operativo il tedesco Markus Krosche, 46 anni, ex Eintracht Francoforte. In Germania ha fatto benissimo, ha sistemi innovativi di valutazione, con una grande rete di scouting. Per gennaio gli obiettivi sono tre, un centravanti dal gol facile, un difensore centrale e un esterno destro di difesa.

Può arrivare Tresoldi? Sarebbe un grande colpo per il Milan, ma anche in chiave nazionale. Il ragazzo, 22 anni, ha sempre tifato i rossoneri. Venire in Italia potrebbe anche convincerlo a scegliere la nazionale azzurra come auspicato da Mancini. Il problema, ovviamente, è il Brugge. La squadra belga chiede una cifra attorno ai sessanta milioni e c’è da verificare la possibilità di trattare già per il mese di gennaio. Su tutto questo stanno lavorando Cardinale e Krosche tenendo aperta anche la porta con il Real Madrid per il brasiliano Endrick, 20 anni.

In questo caso sarebbe una operazione diversa, un prestito con qualche clausola. Il problema è Mourinho che non vuole mai mollare i giocatori anche se li utilizza pochissimo come Endrick. Il ragazzino preme, l’anno scorso a gennaio era stato prestato e vorrebbe una soluzione analoga. In corsa c’è pure la Roma, ma Cardinale da tempo ha aperto un canale con Florentino Perez.

Per il centrale, Amorim ha fatto da tempo il nome del suo preferito: Goncalo Inacio, centrale dello Sporting Lisbona, 25 anni. E’ un difensore dai piedi buoni, capace di guidare la difesa e fare ripartire l’azione, quello che serve al Milan. La valutazione supera i trenta milioni, ma il problema più grosso sembra la resistenza dello Sporting che (per ora) non lo vuole mollare a gennaio. Il filo però non s’è interrotto. L’alternativa è un profilo diverso, Luca Reggiani, 18 anni, strappato dal Borussia Dortmund al Sassuolo. Nazionale under 21, con i tedeschi ha già esordito in prima squadra.

Pensando al futuro, Krosche ha messo pure i riflettori anche su Stiller, regista dello Stoccarda, 25 anni, che ha una clausola da quaranta milioni. Potrebbe essere lui il dopo-Modric. Per il terzo ruolo scoperto, l’esterno destro, è probabile il ritorno anticipato di Athekame, 21 anni, in prestito al Lione dove sta facendo molto bene.

Almeno due anche gli obiettivi della Juve, un attaccante che la metta dentro, come si dice brutalmente, e un esterno sinistro dopo l’ennesimo flop di Cambiaso. Quest’ultimo ruolo potrebbe essere coperto da Aleandro Balde, 23 anni, che nel Barcellona sta trovando poco spazio. La valutazione è molto alta, attorno ai quaranta milioni. Il discorso è aperto. Ma in Spagna la Juve guarda sempre a Sorloth e sta parlando con l’Atletico mettendo sul tavolo la posizione di David che ha soddisfatto Simeone. Sorloth è un uomo d’area, vede la porta al contrario di Waltemade e con lo spostamento di Kolo Muani sulla destra, per caratteristiche sarebbe adattissimo a risolvere il problema vero della Juve: fare gol. Si pensa anche a Scamacca che Carnevali ha avuto al Sassuolo, i dubbi sono sulle sue frequenti ricadute fisiche.

Ma a gennaio si cercherà anche di sfoltire la rosa per recuperare risorse e snellire il lavoro di Spalletti che soprattutto davanti ha una batteria di trequartisti-esterni. Fra l’altro Ildiz dovrebbe rientrare al massimo a inizio anno, quindi gente come Zhegrova potrebbe andare in prestito, ma non solo lui. Oltre a Cambiaso potrebbe partire pure Kelly, ormai finito dietro a Gatti nelle gerarchie spallettiane.

E il Napoli? Inizia la rivoluzione verde. De Laurentiis ha dato via libera a Manna, la rosa va ringiovanita e sfoltita. Inoltre lo spogliatoio andrà liberato di tutti i casi che hanno complicato questo inizio stagione. Non sarà facile trovare una collocazione, ma la lista dei partenti è lunga, da Lucca a Lang, da Beukema a Anguissa che non vuole rinnovare, fino a Neres e Giovane. Manna le proverà tutte per arrivare ai tre giocatori giovani che ha nel mirino, vale a dire Varela, 21 anni, bomber del Monza, Bakola centrocampista del Sassuolo, 19 anni, e Cacciamani esterno del Toro, 19 anni. Varela ha segnato nove gol in dieci partite, il Monza l‘ha pagato due milioni e mezzo dal Benfica e la tentazione di monetizzare subito è forte. La richiesta supera i trenta milioni, ma il rischio di un’altra operazione Piatek frena parecchio gli operatori. Meglio aspettare giugno? L’interrogativo è logico, ma niente è deciso. Difficile, fra l’altro, che Lucca possa eventualmente accettare il prestito al Monza.

Il francese Bakola è stato pagato dieci milioni dal Sassuolo che l’ha strappato al Marsiglia. Ora per venderlo ne servono almeno trenta e c’è pure la concorrenza della Juve che ha (ovviamente) buoni rapporti con la società neroverde. I bianconeri lo vorrebbero acquistare subito per poi lasciarlo a Sassuolo fino a giugno. Alessio Cacciamani è un esterno sinistro tutta fascia. Il Torino chiede venti milioni, è interessata anche la Roma. Anche per questo ragazzo ogni discorso potrebbe essere spostato verso giugno, mentre Allegri ha chiesto rinforzi subito per provare a rimettere in moto il Napoli. Ci riuscirà? De Laurentiis, ovviamente, è deluso dal suo allenatore, ora si aspetta nove punti nelle prossime gare contro Torino, Sassuolo e Lecce. L’allenatore non è in bilico, ma in discussione. Queste tre partite sono una sorta di test, il presidente vuole una reazione forte e ovviamente la vittoria. Se si dovessero riproporre situazioni simili a quelle con il Venezia e altre, allora Allegri potrebbe davvero rischiare un altro esonero nonostante l’ingaggio, il licenziamento costerebbe infatti una cifra-monstre tra i venticinque e i trenta milioni.

#2080. Former Stoke City and Swansea City midfielder completes move to National League promotion hopefuls

Worthing currently sit 6th in the National League table and are eyeing up promotion to the Football League for the first time in their history. Now, they have strengthened their midfield by signing former Stoke City and Swansea City star Sam Clucas, who brings a huge amount of experience to the team.

The 36-year-old was last contracted to Shrewsbury Town, where he played 34 league fixtures last season, scoring two goals and assisting five. He was an important player in the Shrews’ squad last campaign, but his services were not extended further following the summer.

Across his career, Clucas has played in the Premier League, Championship, League One and League Two, and has featured for a multitude of clubs. Hereford, Mansfield Town, Chesterfield, Hull City, Swansea City, Stoke City, Rotherham United, Oldham Athletic, Lincoln City, Shrewsbury Town and now Worthing are the clubs Clucas has represented.

The experienced EFL star will now prepare for life in the fifth tier, with the hope of bringing an historic promotion to the Reds. Worthing are currently in the play-offs, having lost just one league match in their last 11.

Clucas’ experience will be worth its weight in gold, and he has a clear hunger to deliver success to Worthing. “I can see the vision of the club, and I want to be a part of it,” he said in the club statement confirming his arrival.

The former Premier League footballer has plied his trade in the most competitive division in the world and will bring a calm and level head to the National League side, especially as the pressure ramps up later on in the season.

The ex-Stoke City and Swansea City man has already made his debut too. He came on off the bench on Saturday as the Rebels drew 1-1 with Scunthorpe United.

Clucas has penned a one-year deal with the non-league side, but could be offered longer terms if he impresses at the club. If the move proves to be a success, then Worthing will try to tie him down for longer and prolong his playing career.

But if the former Stoke City and Swansea City man fails to hit the heights expected of him, the Reds will not be hurt by his departure next summer, given his contract length.

He has shown he can still play plenty of games after featuring 40 times across the 2025/26 campaign for Shrewsbury Town. Clucas appears to have plenty left in the tank, and he will help to bring squad depth to Worthing as the busiest time of the footballing calendar nears.

#2078. Bristol City size up managerial candidates despite recent Michael Skubala statement

Bristol City sit 17th in the Championship table after winning only one of their last seven Championship games. Michael Skubala has come under fire with some early calls for his sacking, but chief executive Charlie Boss stated that the summer appointment will be given time to turn around the Robins’ fortunes.

Now though, reporter Alan Nixon states that City are doing background checks on potential replacements if they are forced into a decision over Skubala’s future. The hierarchy are checking into the availability and cost of possible targets, and there are funds in place to pay compensation for an in-work target.

Although the Robins have stated Skubala is getting a chance to find form, the belief is that they should be far higher up the Championship table. If form doesn’t turn and the right replacement candidate is up for grabs, the former Lincoln City boss could be moved on.

Boss didn’t say how long Skubala has got to turn around his fortunes to offer any hints untoward, but the fact that the pressure has been publicly addressed shows that Bristol City are acutely aware that they need to be doing far better than they are at present.

Unfortunately for Skubala, in the bid to find form, he’s got some tough opponents to face. Kim Hellberg’s Middlesbrough are up first after the ongoing international break ends, before an important home match against Wrexham the following Tuesday.

The Robins are back on the road at another promotion hopeful afterwards as they head to The Hawthorns to face West Brom. December then begins with a home tie against Swansea City, with clashes against Derby County and West Ham (both away) following.

It marks a tough run of fixtures for Skubala as he desperately looks to find the form to secure his Ashton Gate position.

Bristol City have a squad capable of far more than 17th in the Championship. The likes of Scott Twine and Jason Knight are both star players at this level, while Rio Cardines has impressed on loan from Crystal Palace and big money was spent on Dom Ballard and Lorent Tolaj.

It means that pressure on Skubala is justified, but the club are taking a smart approach in holding fire on sacking the boss for now. With new chief executive Boss, sporting director James Ellis and the new manager, it is the start of a real refresh at Ashton Gate as they hope to build towards long-term success.

A lot of work went into hiring Skubala from Lincoln City as they deduced him to be the perfect candidate to lead this new chapter. More was expected of the manager in the short term, but he will be judged on long-term results, so it is only right that he is given time to get out of this rut.

If it comes as any reassurance, Skubala endured a tough start with Lincoln. He won only two of his first 14 games, but he was given time to recover and built them into a League One title-winning side.

Bristol City will hope for a similar turnaround, but if it doesn’t come, they will be ready to act.

#2074. Two positions West Ham boss Scott Parker wants to strengthen in the January transfer window

West Ham opted for change earlier this month as they parted ways with Nuno Espirito Santo to bring in Scott Parker as boss. The former three-time WHUFC Player of the Year will be expected to deliver improvements with his current squad, but new signings will be sought in the winter transfer window too.

According to Alan Nixon, the Hammers’ boss is eager to add new options at left-back and striker when January comes around. His preference is to sign a centre-forward with Championship experience, while a ‘specialist’ is left full-back is sought given that Morato is primarily a centre-back while Ezra Mayers and Ollie Scarles are only young.

Parker has tasked scouts with finding standout targets in both positions and the money is there to spend. It remains to be seen just who emerges on the radar with around six weeks until the window opens.

Parker hasn’t even been at West Ham for two weeks, but he already has a good idea of where they need to strengthen if they are to achieve their goal of promotion back to the Premier League.

And, with reinforcements sought at striker and left-back, many supporters will be behind the boss too. Striker has been a problem area with none of Joel Piroe, Taty Castellanos or Pablo proving they can be the Hammers’ leading talisman as of yet.

There are options at left-back, but Morato felt very much like a Nuno player given their past spell together at Nottingham Forest. His defence-first game suited the former boss’ style too.

Youngsters Mayers and Scarles may hope to prove they can step up for Parker, but a specialist left-back would not go amiss. It could also mean the writing is on the wall for Adama Boiro, who has not played since his debut on September 5th.

Parker has won three promotions from the Championship, and he is targeting a fourth with West Ham. Given his past success, the club hierarchy will be more than willing to put faith in his transfer opinions ahead of January.

WHUFC seem set to heed his advice and target reinforcements at both striker and left-back ahead of January. There are already plenty of players in these positions, but with neither locked down by a clear standout, there is a need for ruthlessness in upgrading in both areas.

Not only will it strengthen the squad, but it will help Parker make his mark too. Players signed specifically for his setup and tactics will be backed to come in and make a swift impact as the Hammers take action in the bid to win promotion.

#2073. GdS: Tactics, data and team-mates – the ‘strange case’ of Goncalo Ramos at Milan

The Goncalo Ramos enigma continues to dominate the newspaper columns, as AC Milan try unlock their record signing.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport report, Milan fans hoped they had finally found a top-class striker in Ramos, but his three goals this season are not sufficient compared to expectations and the €70m price tag for which he arrived.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

And yet, the Portuguese centre-forward is still proving to be a factor in the team’s fortunes. The reason for this lies behind statistics that the average fan might ignore, but Ruben Amorim certainly isn’t.

The coach has repeatedly emphasised how Ramos is helping the team, less so the other way around. Looking at the numbers, you can’t argue with him. Gonçalo may not be making it into the top scorers’ table, but his work is well explained by statistics that place him among the top strikers in Serie A.

Which ones? Passes (20.7 per game, first in volume among centre-forwards in the league ahead of Lazio’s Noslin) or touches (2nd), for example. But also the aerial duels won and fouls drawn (19, first among attackers) underscore the importance of his sacrifice too.

There are two considerations that don’t emerge from the statistics, but are equally important. The first concerns the movements that free up or facilitate team-mates, such as the sprint for Milan’s first goal in Genoa.

Alphadjo Cisse found himself all alone in the penalty area thanks to Ramos drawing two of the Rossoblu central defenders towards him, allowing Adrien Rabiot to easily pass to the young Italian who was in lots of space.

The second consideration concerns the pressure and coverage work, which has changed since the start of the season. In the early days, Gonçalo was the first to apply pressure up front, but in doing so, he exposed Modric to too much space to cover in front of or behind him.

Amorim therefore asked the Portuguese to instead harass the opposing playmaker, without attacking the defence in the initial possession. This move allows Luka to run less and think more during the opponent’s possession phase.

We were talking about a Milan side that is helping Ramos less than the centre-forward is helping the team, too. The former Benfica man is 19th in Serie A for shots (26) and 15th for shots on target (10).

While it’s true that the Rossoneri maintain a high standard in terms of the quality of chances created (third in the league for big chances behind Inter and Roma), it’s equally undeniable that they arrive in the final third of the pitch less often than expected. Milan are 12th for touches in the opponent’s penalty area and 12th for shots on target.

In short, Ramos sees the ball mostly where he can’t hurt the goalkeepers. Even if, in relation to goal-scoring chances, he should have scored double in the league: 4.16 xG compared to the just two scored. Still, not enough for a Milan-calibre player.

#2071. £3.5m man needs Ipswich Town exit: Birmingham City & Stoke City must plan move

The January transfer window is fast approaching, and as the new year draws closer, transfer news will begin to ramp up, with one Ipswich Town player almost certain to return to the English second tier this winter.

The two-week international break has given Championship clubs, and the rest of Europe, a chance to reassess their current situations and squads ahead of the upcoming festive period.

The weeks leading into the new year are especially busy for teams across the EFL, who must contend with immense fixture congestion, as whilst the work on the pitch will be almost non-stop, so will the work off of it, with the January transfer window right around the corner.

Plans for the winter window will almost certainly already be being put in place by clubs across the continent, with the English second tier being no different, as one player will surely be on the shortlist of almost every club in the division heading into the new year.

Football League World has asked AI to rank the top nine toughest fanbases in the EFL Championship right now from least to most

Anis Mehmeti joined Ipswich Town from Bristol City in January 2026 for around £3.5 million, having announced himself as one of the best attacking midfielders in the division over the past couple of years at Ashton Gate.

Mehmeti, 25, was the subject of interest from numerous clubs in the Championship over the summer window, with Pete O'Rourke reporting on Birmingham City's and Wrexham's interest in the Albanian, whilst Alan Nixon reported via his Patreon on Derby County's pursuit.

Anis Mehmeti Championship statistics 2025/26 (Data from FotMob)

The attacking midfielder ultimately opted to remain in Suffolk and fight for his place in the Premier League under new boss Gary O'Neil, but after ten gameweeks, he has yet to make a single matchday squad in the top flight.

Mehmeti cannot afford to be sat in the stands much longer and let an entire season of football pass him by, as Football League World has taken a look at two Championship clubs that must look to strike an agreement with the Tractor Boys this January to bring him back to the EFL.

Birmingham City have previously been credited with an interest in Mehmeti as recently as last summer, and it would be no surprise to see Chris Davies' side head back into the market for him again.

Jay Stansfield has more often than not been used in the number ten role in Davies' preferred 4-2-3-1 shape at St Andrews, though in recent weeks, Max Bird has been pushed further forward as Stansfield deputises up top in the absence of August Priske.

An injury to either Stansfield or Bird would all of a sudden see Davies scrambling for options in that area of the pitch, and having registered an interest in Portsmouth's Adrian Segecic in the summer as well, another option at attacking midfield heading to the Second City this winter wouldn't come as a surprise to anyone.

Mehmeti, whilst best through the middle, can play anywhere across the final third, and though Birmingham can boast the likes of Carlos Vicente, Patrick Roberts, Demarai Gray, and Liam Millar out wide, adding Mehmeti to the mix only creates more competition and ups everyone's game.

The Blues head into the international break sitting pretty at the top of the Championship table with a superior goal difference over Middlesbrough and Stoke City, who they are level on points with, as automatic promotion looks like a real possibility this year.

Bringing in Mehmeti could be the final piece of the puzzle Davies needs to secure a historic year for Birmingham, who must go all out to secure his services in January.

Where do you think Mehmeti should go in January, and where do you think he will go? Would you like to see him at your club? Share your thoughts below!

Stoke City, like Birmingham, find themselves in a promotion battle this year after an excellent start to the campaign.

The Potters, despite losing each of their three opening fixtures to Swansea City, Southampton, and Wolverhampton Wanderers, have bounced back with just one defeat in their last 12 league games, winning nine, as no team in the Championship has won more games than Mark Robins' side at this stage.

It's a miraculous turnaround in form from Stoke, who enjoyed an equally excellent beginning to last season as well, as this time around, Robins will have no intention of dropping off as they previously have.

Switching to a 3-4-2-1 shape, this system change has been the catalyst for their rise up the league table, with Jack McGlynn shining in one of the attacking midfield roles, Ethan Galbraith dictating games from deeper, and Viktor Johansson consistently keeping the scoreline down in goal.

McGlynn has been an almost ever-present in that role since his introduction to the side, though alongside him, Bae Jun-ho, Justin Devenny, and Million Manhoef have each been used, but none of them has been able to nail down a place in the starting XI.

With Bae out of contract at the end of the season, a January exit wouldn't be a shock, as Stoke can kill two birds with one stone by shifting the Korean and upgrading with Mehmeti.

If the North Staffordshire outfit are still in a battle for promotion, they must go all out to get over the line, as Mehmeti could help the Potters to secure a memorable year.

#2070. AFC Wimbledon vs Blackpool “shouldn’t have taken place”, says Ian Evatt after sickness-hit squad loses 1-0

Blackpool fell to a narrow 1-0 defeat against fellow strugglers AFC Wimbledon, with Alistair Smith netting the all-important goal in the 13th minute with a sublime strike from distance.

To say the Tangerines’ preparations for the trip to South London were disrupted would be an understatement. Ian Evatt’s group was ravaged by a sickness bug, leaving 14 players and staff absent. Bailey Peacock-Farrell and Josh Bowler, two positives in an otherwise tough campaign, were two notable absentees at Plough Lane.

Speaking after the game, Evatt admitted he had never encountered anything quite like it as he spoke to the club’s media channels. He said: “I don’t want to be stood here and feel like I am making excuses; I can only tell the truth. We’ve had 14 players and staff have severe diarrhoea and vomiting for the last 24 hours – it started as soon as we got on the train yesterday, and it spiralled quickly.

“Some players and staff haven’t been able to get out of bed, but they put themselves forward to come on the pitch and play today. For me, we’ve been put in a position we shouldn’t have been put into and this game shouldn’t have taken place today and I would have been saying that if we had won the game.”

The game had a COVID-19 feel with the two sides emerging from the tunnel separately and skipping the customary pre-match handshakes.

Nonetheless, Evatt’s Blackpool dominated for large spells and should have taken at least a point back up to Lancashire, but they couldn’t beat the inspired Nathan Bishop in the Dons’ net.

The energetic performance was a testament to the character of Blackpool in challenging circumstances. They mustered 15 attempts on goal compared to AFC Wimbledon’s nine and created over double their opponents’ xG at 1.22 (FotMob).

They failed to take advantage of the several opportunities they had though, with Dale Taylor and Tom Bloxham struggling to make an impact leading the line.

Returning to Bloomfield Road last October after seven years as a player, Evatt is arguably facing one of his most challenging periods in the dugout.

He managed to steer Blackpool away from relegation last term, although not convincingly, but inconsistency this term has once again left them languishing at the wrong end of the table.

Following a bright start with wins over Stockport County and Peterborough United, a run of just one victory in 10 league outings has put the Seasiders in a very familiar position and staring down the barrel of another relegation dogfight.

Evatt raised his stock considerably at Bolton Wanderers but is yet to make his mark at Blackpool, with the visit of in-form Wigan Athletic next Saturday potentially proving decisive in his long-term future.

#2069. Repubblica: Milan and Real Madrid watching as Napoli star McTominay stalls on contract

Scott McTominay’s Napoli future is in doubt, and a report has named AC Milan among the surprise potential suitors.

In a Napoli side that appears to have lost its way, one of the few lights leading the way remains McTominay. Despite a season that started on the wrong foot and a heart condition (now resolved), the Scot has five goals in 11 games this season across Serie A and the Champions League.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Massimiliano Allegri’s team is going through a tough time, and the former Manchester United player himself has had some tough nights. As La Repubblica (via Calciomercato.com) report, Napoli fans are beginning to worry about where things are heading.

The 29-year-old McTominay is at a turning point in his career, one which has been revitalised since his arrival at Napoli and the Scudetto won under Antonio Conte. His current contract with the Neapolitans expires in 2028, but negotiations for a renewal have stalled.

Fabrizio Romano reported that Napoli remain confident in the possibility of reaching an agreement over an extension, but the uncertainty currently surrounding the project, the bad results and doubts about the club’s future are forcing him to evaluate.

La Repubblica add that the discussions have even stalled after positive steps were taken in September. McTominay and his representatives want to better understand the Azzurri’s vision moving forward before finalising a new agreement.

Sky Switzerland journalist Sacho Tavolieri reported that the former Manchester United man’s agent has already held discussions with several English clubs. Napoli have not completely ruled out a possible sale, and the figure would be €25-30m.

His contract is currently worth €4.5m net per season. Napoli would like to extend it until 2030 with a salary increase, but they are unwilling to accept the Scotsman’s demands, who has requested around €7-8m net per season.

According to La Repubblica, at the end of the season McTominay and Napoli will sit down to discuss the terms of the new contract, once the club’s plans are clearer. Several clubs are interested though and are watching closely.

Aston Villa and Manchester United enquired in the summer. In the coming weeks, Real Madrid and AC Milan will also be keeping a close eye on the developments surrounding McTominay.

The Rossoneri are currently well-stocked in midfield with Luka Modric, Adrien Rabiot, Yunus Musah, Ardon Jashari plus options like Ruben Loftus-Cheek and the young Christian Comotto. However, with Amorim at the helm, the prospect of profound change is never far away.

#2068. Major Sheffield Wednesday v Plymouth Argyle flashpoint causes big online stir

Sheffield Wednesday fans went home happy on Saturday, as they cruised to a comfortable 3-0 win over fellow promotion-chasing side, Plymouth Argyle.

It was the perfect start to life in charge of the Owls in League One for Dave Challinor, who picked up three points at the first available opportunity in front of the Owls supporters.

Billy Mitchell opened the scoring on the day for Sheffield Wednesday, which came just before the half-time whistle. Davis Keillor-Dunn and Di'Shon Bernard then added two late goals to secure an eye-catching win at Hillsborough.

Bernard's goal late on was the pick of the bunch, as he fired home in emphatic style from distance, much to the surprise and delight of the home crowd.

The result means that Sheffield Wednesday moved ahead of Plymouth in the table, and up to fifth, as they look to finish in the top-six in League One this term.

One of the main talking points from the win over Tom Cleverley's side wasn't any of the goals on the day though, as a poor challenge from Plymouth's Ronan Curtis only saw a yellow card awarded to the winger.

Ronan Curtis' challenge on Jamal Lowe was at chest height, and the Hillsborough crowd were left furious that only a yellow card was awarded, with many feeling as though there wasn't any other option than a red card.

Lowe was able to carry on and play on, before being substituted for Liam Palmer with five minutes remaining in the match, and he'll be hoping he can kick on and feature for the Owls in their bid for promotion.

Curtis didn't appear to be looking at Lowe beforehand, and some Plymouth fans came to their player's defence for the incident which sparked plenty of debate on social media.

The Plymouth winger was apologetic after it occurred, but it certainly endangered Lowe with his boot being so high off the ground, and so there was real surprise to only see a yellow card shown by the referee.

Do you think it should have been a no-brainer for Curtis' challenge to be worthy of a red card instead of a yellow?

Speaking to The Star after the win over Plymouth, newly-appointed Sheffield Wednesday boss Dave Challinor issued his verdict on the challenge from Curtis, and felt as though it was right to appeal for a red card.

"Well, it's definitely chest high. I think you're always going to appeal for it. I think Tom (Cleverley) would have been appealing for it exactly the same, and he was open to that. What do you need to do? What constitutes a red card? If it catches him on the jaw, did Ronan Curtis mean it? I'd probably suggest no."

The ball's coming over his shoulder, but if one of our players would have done that, I would have been fearing the worst. Thankfully, it didn't make a huge impact at the end of the game."

"He (referee) said there was, I think, minimal force. I suggest if it's you on the end of it, it might have a different thought. It's high. It's probably one of them ones you toss a coin, 50% of referees flash a red without even thinking."

Sheffield Wednesday are now in the play-off positions, and will fancy their chances of remaining in there for the foreseeable future if they can replicate a similar level of performance.

#2067. 25-year-old must come straight into the Derby County XI amid positive injury update: Opinion

Derby County have had a tough season to date, but they entered the international break on a high by beating Bolton Wanderers 3-1 at Pride Park. It gives DCFC fans some renewed hope, and might have saved John Eustace his job as well.

The Rams have been way under par, but injuries have torn through the squad and played a big part in their struggles. Eustace’s defence has been heavily impacted especially, and among those sidelined has been Eiran Cashin.

But, in a welcome boost, the Brighton & Hove Albion loanee has been back in training over the first week of the international break. Cashin may need a little more time before he gets back to full fitness, but once deemed ready, he should come straight back into their starting lineup.

Cashin was a popular signing in the summer transfer window. The 25-year-old is a product of the Derby County academy and left to join Brighton in January 2025, but has struggled to make the grade at the Premier League club and spent spells on loan back in the Championship as a result.

He didn’t impress as hoped at Birmingham City, but offered a timely reminder of how good he can be at the level during his stay at Blackburn Rovers. Cashin helped the Lancashire outfit steer clear of relegation last season before reuniting with the Rams for the 2026/27 campaign.

The Irishman has only played twice for DCFC since his return due to this calf injury, but he will be backed to land a key role when fit and available. He’s a dependable and busy defender at this level, with his 3.26 tackles per 90 last season more than any other Championship defender.

Cashin also managed 12.96 defensive contributions, 9.33 duels won, and 14.94 line-breaking passes per 90, ranking among the league’s best in these metrics too (FotMob). He’ll offer Eustace an option at left-back and centre-back, and give the boss the option to switch to a back three as well.

He will bring more balance to the backline as a left-footer and has the love for defending that has been coached out of some modern-day centre-backs.

The Bolton Wanderers win was only one victory, but it will hopefully mark a big step in the right direction. It lifts a weight off the shoulders of Eustace and his Derby County players coming into the break.

This paired with the improving injury picture should give DCFC hope that they can start to find some form. Not only is Cashin back in training, but Patrick Agyemang and Matt Clarke featured in the behind-closed-doors friendly at Everton on Thursday as well.

With defensive depth and key players returning, the Rams will be targeting some valuable points to push up the Championship table and away from the relegation zone.

#2066. Fresh £30m-40m claim made on Birmingham City ace Jay Stansfield

A fresh claim has been made over the importance of Jay Stansfield to Chris Davies' Birmingham City side, with the club's record signing currently enjoying a strong patch of form.

The 23-year-old's time at St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park has garnered plenty of attention ever since he was lured back to the club two summers ago for an eye-catching fee in excess of £15m from Premier League side, Fulham, on a seven-year contract.

Stansfield has since become the 'poster boy' of Knighthead Capital Management's ambitious rebuild in this part of the world, and that has brought its own advantages and pressures.

After recently surpassing 150 appearances in royal blue, the England youth international striker's brace against Swansea City last Saturday was enough to see him become the latest player to have scored 50 goals in all competitions for the club and send Davies' side top of the Championship.

Stansfield's current form is a stark contrast to the frustrations which he endured last term whilst adapting to a new role within Davies' setup, and with that being said, Football League World quizzed our Birmingham City fan pundit, Jason Moore, if the attacker is deemed 'untouchable' in January.

Stansfield was one of two Birmingham players who reached double-figures last season, albeit two of his 11 goals came after the turn of the year, leaving question marks over his performance levels and output.

It was then claimed in the summer that the forward was the subject of interest from clubs such as Everton, Hull City, Ipswich Town and Sunderland, with Stansfield's reported valuation coming in at the £25m mark as a result.

Oliver Glasner's side are reportedly interested in acquiring Phil Neumann from the Championship leaders

The forward later reaffirmed his commitment to the cause at St. Andrew's, although it was widely debated whether Birmingham should have potentially considered moving on their prized asset for said price.

Birmingham have seen goals fly in from all angles so far this season, with Davies' tactical reshuffles certainly getting the best out of Patrick Roberts, Liam Millar, Stansfield and August Priske in recent weeks.

Priske has netted six goals so far this season, but his absence in the victories over Millwall and Swansea allowed Stansfield to return to the main striking role, scoring three times in 180 minutes' worth of action, taking his seasonal tally to four strikes and one assist.

As such, Moore believes that even more would need to be coughed up if suitors were to even attempt prizing him away from B9.

"I got asked the same question in the August transfer window and back then I said 'take what you can get for him, go and reinvest in the squad', but I just can't do it," he told FLW.

"He's 'Blues', he gets what we're about, and I don't think you'll find a Blues fan that's got a bad word to say about him now. I was calling to probably sell him, but no, keep him. He is 'Mr Birmingham' at the moment.

Blues fans, how do you rate Jay Stansfield's season so far /10? Comment below!

"He's not scoring goals, but he just works so hard for the team, and he's literally just what we're about," Moore added.

"He's pivotal to what Chris Davies is doing with the way we're playing. So no, and I know I'm going to sound ridiculous here, but unless you're giving us like £30-40m no, I don't want him gone.

"You might get some fans who say 'that's silly, take £20m', not for me. I love him so much, I'd rather just find the money another way and keep him."

Stansfield's importance to Blues right now is way beyond his goalscoring exploits, even though some would still expect a strong return given his price tag.

Emphasising such a viewpoint, Davies recently said of the forward: "As a manager, you always go with the ones that you know are going to give everything, and one thing with him is, he gives absolutely everything in every game."

#2064. Sheffield Wednesday owner David Storch must watch Josh Windass situation

A new era is underway at Sheffield Wednesday following the appointment of Dave Challinor as the club's new manager.

Wednesday made the decision to part company with Henrik Pedersen last month following an inconsistent start to life back in League One, and Challinor has been tasked with getting their promotion push back on track.

Challinor had been out of work since leaving Stockport County in June after a near five-year spell at Edgeley Park, during which time he led the Hatters from the National League to League One, and his side missed out on promotion to the Championship in his final game as they were beaten by Bolton Wanderers in last season's play-off final.

The 51-year-old, who has also had spells with the likes of AFC Fylde and Hartlepool United, boasts the incredible record of finishing in the play-offs or higher in each of his 15 full seasons as a manager, winning promotion on seven occasions.

Challinor will be looking to add an eighth promotion to his CV with Wednesday this season, but given that the club were forced to operate under transfer restrictions in the summer as the consequences of Dejphon Chansiri's disastrous reign continue to bite, there are question marks over whether the current squad is good enough to secure a return to the Championship.

It is unclear when the remaining constraints on the Owls will be lifted, but once they are able to spend freely, owner David Storch should consider making an ambitious move for one of the club's former fan favourites.

While Storch's takeover marked the start of a bright new era at Hillsborough, Wednesday turned to a few familiar faces this summer as they rebuilt their squad.

Midfielder Barry Bannan achieved club legend status during a 10-and-a-half year spell with the Owls after arriving on a free transfer from Crystal Palace in 2015, but, amid the off-field uncertainty, he departed for Millwall in January.

However, after less than six months at The Den, Bannan made an emotional return to Wednesday in July, and the deal was a clear indication of the fact that Storch and the new hierarchy were keen not to distance themselves too much from the club's past.

Bannan was not the only ex-Owls star to re-join the club this summer, with goalkeeper Joe Lumley and defender Reece James, who was part of the squad that won promotion from League One in the 2022-23 season, also returning for second stints in South Yorkshire.

Of course, Storch should not rely too heavily on sentimental signings, and Bannan's somewhat underwhelming start to the campaign proves that it can be difficult to recapture previous magic, but he should weigh up a swoop for forward Josh Windass if Challinor succeeds in leading Wednesday to promotion this season.

Windass spent five-and-a-half years with Wednesday after joining from Wigan Athletic in January 2020, scoring 53 goals and providing 23 assists in 182 appearances in all competitions, including a 123rd-minute winner in the play-off final against Barnsley at Wembley in 2023 to seal the club's promotion to the Championship.

However, as the scale of the Owls' crisis under Chansiri became clear last summer, Windass opted to terminate his contract at Hillsborough, and he subsequently made the move to Championship newcomers Wrexham.

Windass enjoyed an outstanding debut campaign at the SToK Cae Ras last season, scoring 16 goals and registering seven assists in 46 appearances in all competitions, but it was not enough to help the Red Dragons into the play-offs as they missed out on the top six on the final day.

It has been a frustrating start to the current season for Windass, with the 32-year-old registering just one assist in six appearances during what has been an injury-hit start to the campaign, and his absence has certainly been felt by Phil Parkinson's side.

Given his importance to the team, Wrexham would likely be reluctant to allow Windass to leave next summer, but should Wednesday win promotion to the Championship, there is no doubt that the forward would be an exciting signing to kickstart the next phase of the Storch era.

Windass still regularly references his former club on social media, most recently taking to Instagram to react to the appointment of his ex-Rangers team-mate Clint Hill as Challinor's assistant, which suggests that he does still hold plenty of affection for the Owls and may well be open to a potential return.

Should Sheffield Wednesday bring Josh Windass back to Hillsborough in the future or is it time to move on? Tell us in the comments below!

#2063. The 3 summer targets West Ham should pursue again in January, including a new Arne Engels midfield partner

West Ham currently sit 9th in the Championship table following the sacking of Nuno Espirito Santo and hiring of Scott Parker. WHUFC will hope the three-time promotion-winning boss can deliver the same success after his spells at Burnley, Bournemouth and Fulham.

However, the squad also needs refreshing when the January transfer window comes around. The defence has been heavily criticised and is sure to be an area targeted for reinforcements by the Hammers.

New targets will be on the radar, but West Ham identified some smart options in the summer who could be available this winter. Here, we put forward three summer transfer targets who should be back on their radar ahead of January…

For all of West Ham’s attacking success this season, their defence has been a concern. Konstantinos Mavropanos has chipped in with five goals as a set-piece threat, but defensively, he and Max Kilman have left a lot to be desired.

Mavropanos is the subject of persisting interest from the likes of Besiktas. A new centre-back may be needed regardless of what comes of the Greek defender’s situation, and Axel Disasi should be on the radar.

Disasi has endured a tough start to life at Crystal Palace and rumours are circulating about an early departure from the Premier League. Should he do so, a return to WHUFC could benefit all parties.

West Ham have endured uncertainty in midfield for a while, with the futures of Edson Alvarez and Soungoutou Magassa up in the air. Arne Engels has been the only regular in the midfield, but he needs a partner who can offer a powerful presence alongside him.

Nelson Deossa was targeted by WHUFC in the summer, and he can be the answer to their midfield problems. The Colombian has played sixteen matches so far for Real Betis this season and is under contract until 2030.

Tomas Soucek has served as a key physical asset in midfield, but a long-term heir for his role is needed. Deossa would bring strength, power and work rate, as well as a well-rounded game in possession with regard to his passing and ball carrying.

A January deal could be tough given Deossa’s calibre and the Hammers’ status in the Championship, but it would be an ambitious and exciting move for the club to make.

One of West ham’s defensive issues this season has been at left-back. Nuno favoured Morato in that position while Ollie Scarles has had opportunities and Ezra Mayers is breaking through, but no one has really made that spot their own.

One man who could be an immediate fix is Matt Targett, who starred in the Championship with Middlesbrough last season. The Englishman’s move to Hull City has not worked out and a winter change of scenery could be just what he needs.

WHUFC could land a quick fix at left-back with Targett while youngsters Mayers and Scarles find opportunities as backup and competition.

#2062. ‘Not ready’, ‘out of control’ and ‘the end of the world’: What Amorim’s words tell us about Milan’s state

Ruben Amorim is not one to hold back when it comes to speaking his thoughts to the media, and the last few days are no exception.

The past week or so has seen Amorim have to digest the best and worst of his AC Milan side. The 3-1 derby win over Inter generated a euphoria that begun whispers of the word ‘Scudetto’, before a dismal defeat to Ferencvaros which saw Milan drop to 29th in the Europa League standings.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This rollercoaster of extremes didn’t stop either side of those two games either. Before the victory over the Nerazzurri a 2-1 lead had been coughed up against Bologna, who scored three times in the second half to win at San Siro and inflict the first league defeat on the Rossoneri.

Yesterday, the Diavolo responded to the season low-point against the Hungarians by beating a Genoa side that had won their last three games and four of their last five. This Milan team is a very difficult one to work out, and it seems even the manager is struggling to do so.

After the Ferencvaros and Genoa games, we learned a lot about where Amorim sees his team to be at. Some key lines from his post-match comments demonstrated a wide spectrum of reaction, from anger to pride, passing through encouragement and worry.

Ruben Amorim has often gone to bat for his players after negative performances and results this season, but it seems that the defeat on Thursday night had pushed his patience to the brink as he tore into his team after the game.

“There’s no explanation. There’s nothing I can say, especially about the first half. I don’t remember another first half like it. It’s about ambition, concentration, desire,” he said.

“We gave away opportunities, we gave away stupid gifts. We weren’t prepared to play football tonight. I usually have a lot to say in defence of our team, but not tonight. We need to be more humble and understand what happened.”

For the first time we saw a peek behind the mask, one that has very often been one portraying an optimistic and positive expression. Amorim knew there was no point attempting to lie to the supporters, the media but above all to himself.

What we know is that Amorim echoed the ferocity of these sentiments when speaking in the dressing room after full-time in what was likely the first dressing down that the team got. Six players were reported to have disappointed more than the others, too.

Above all, what stood out was the fact that the head coach opted to question whether his players wanted it enough. This was no longer a question of learning an identity, rotation or an injury crisis: it became a matter of heart.

Another intriguing extract from the post-Ferencvaros tirade that Amorim went on was about the squad’s ability to balance playing in two different competitions, namely Serie A and the Europa League.

“We’re not ready to be competitive on two fronts. We need to work on our way of looking at football and how we approach matches. There are no excuses tonight, there’s nothing I can say.

“I have to focus on the league, obviously, but we also have to do well in the Europa League. We must and can win games despite the rotation. We have to be ready – we’re not now – to play and win every three days.

“But I won’t give up on this competition. But as long as the mathematics don’t condemn us, we’ll fight in this competition as we do in the others.”

Once again, Amorim offered a bit of a revelation: the league is the absolute priority for Milan this season. It may not exactly be revolutionary information, given that a top four spot remains the most accessible avenue to the main objective for 2026-27: securing a Champions League return.

And yet, in his emotional outburst, the former Sporting CP and Manchester United boss told us all in black and white that Serie A will be the focus. As a result, it’s right to expect more ups and downs in Europe, especially with such a depleted squad.

There is an element of observational realism about Amorim’s words; almost an admission of defeat in his attempts to spin two plates at the same time and get the most out of the resources at his disposal. Does it suggest a Europa League resurgence is coming? Not exactly.

Amorim has not made a habit of mentioning individuals ever since his arrivals, both in his pre-match words but especially after games in which emotions are running high. However, he brought up someone who was absent for the Ferencvaros game.

“Everyone needs to train like Pavlovic. He’s ready to die in training. He’s a good example. Sometimes when players don’t start, they struggle. But there are no excuses, we should have won even with those who started,” he said.

Going into the season there were some who were legitimately questioning whether Strahinja Pavlovic would even be a tactical fit for Amorim’s usual 3-4-2-1 system, given that he prefers more composed, ball-playing outside centre-backs.

The answer to those doubts is that in November the Serbian has become the shining light in the eyes of his manager. We mentioned earlier that it had become a question of heart, and nobody can doubt that Pavlovic has that in abundance.

For all of the talk about tactics, systems, shapes and patterns, football is a simple game that very often comes down to who wants it more. In this regard, Amorim elevated Pavlovic as the example to follow, while hoping he returns from injury for the Frosinone game after the break.

Moving on to the post-Genoa reflections, what was quite apparent was that Ruben Amorim was in no mood to get carried away. In fact, if anything, he revealed his belief that his team are still miles off where he wants them.

“What I feel is that, when we’re competitive, we’re difficult to beat, and now we’re steering the game towards our style. We push for control with the ball.

“When we’re not able to be competitive, we’re completely out of control. It’s a big difference, but it’s something we need to work on. But again, the team’s evolution, the way we’re playing, is completely different from the start of the season, and I’m happy with that.

“We should have more points. I’m clearly not happy with the European games, not just because of the results, but because of the performance. Results can happen, but the performances are far from what we want. However, I think we’ll be a better team in the future.”

So, for now this version of Milan is not one that satisfies the coach. The words are a good summary of what the last six games have shown, in which there have been an even split of victories and defeats: on their day the team can beat anyone in the league, but on an off-day they can lose to anyone too.

What Amorim seems keen to hammer home is that progress for this season will be judged on the ability to bring the ceiling closer to the floor. In other words, we have seen the potential of this team already with some impressive wins, yet the base level for performances remains frighteningly low.

Consistency is not just about being able to string together several positive results in a row, something the current Rossoneri do not seem capable of. It is about the repeated displaying of an idea and an identity every few days, to suggest the team are getting closer to the vision the coach has.

Various things make that difficult (perhaps unachievable, based on Amorim’s other comments) right now, such as the injury situation and the multiple windows needed to sculpt the squad. Progress is not always linear, but the target has been set.

One of the themes that Amorim has been consistently questioned on this season is how to unlock the club-record signing Goncalo Ramos, who remains stuck on three goals (one of which was a penalty).

After the Genoa game, he said: “I think we’re lacking time in the final third. We control the ball away from the opponent’s penalty area. This is also key for Goncalo Ramos to have more clear-cut chances. It’s clearly not Goncalo’s fault.

“Pulisic is far from the penalty area. Gonçalo is far from the penalty area. All these players play away from the penalty area, so I can say we’re still far from the final product, because we’re still working on good progression, but then in the final third of the pitch we waste a lot of time with the ball there.”

This is one of the points of ‘evolution’ that Amorim clearly wants to see from his side, but is yet to achieve. Milan are not yet a team that can sustain pressure in the opposition half, nor can they penetrate the box with any regularity either.

In fact, a report from Sky backed this up with some interesting numbers, look specifically at data per 30 minutes of actual possession. Milan are first in Serie A for build-up actions, but they are 20th for entries into the final third and entries into the opposition box.

Amorim’s side are 19th for percentage of touches in the attacking third and 18th in percentage of touches in the opposition box. When the Rossoneri have the ball, it is rarely in a threatening area.

With numbers like these, there isn’t much for Ramos to get on the end of, and it makes the positive attacking numbers (23 goals in 11 league games) feel quite unsustainable.

The Portuguese striker meanwhile is first in the Milan squad in Serie A for interceptions, recoveries, touches in the middle third and touches in the opposition half. He is second for receptions, touches and duels, and third for passes.

Simply put, the No.9 is being drawn away from the area he should be operating in because the team are not capable of sustaining spells of possession further up the field, so he needs to drop deeper to feel involved.

This is something Amorim must work on, because while the goals are coming from other sources for now – in some cases due to the space Ramos helps create – it could all come tumbling down unless the attacking play improves more generally.

🚨🎙️🛡️ Ruben Amorim on Gonçalo Ramos: “Ramos is helping US more than we are helping him. It’s a TEAM problem, not a Ramos problem.”

“We don’t spend enough time in the final third.”

“When we start keeping the ball there more often, Gonçalo is going to score MANY goals.” pic.twitter.com/b3Zs6YxNym

— Milan Wire (@MilanWireX) November 8, 2026

Finally, we end with what was perhaps the most passionate part of Amorim’s comments following the win at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris on Sunday, again centred around the levels he expects from his team.

“It’s the mentality. When you’re a player, there are no off days. If you play for Milan, for these clubs, there are no off days. You can’t show up like we did on Thursday and then turn it on again for Sunday. It’s not possible, it’s not something that will work.

“It’s not a physical condition, it’s a question of anxiety about defeat. If you ‘panic’ about defeat, it’s not that you’re afraid of losing, but that you know that losing is the end of the world. That’s the feeling I want my teams to have.”

In many ways, the manager was speaking in a way that channels how fans have experienced the past week. How is it possible that Milan can be completely outplayed by a side sat third in the Hungarian lead just days after convincingly beating the Italian champions?

Against Genoa, how can the team play as they did in the first half, and then appear to completely drop off a cliff in the second half when the time came to dig deep and bring the result home? The disparity in levels both in-game and from match to match is astounding everyone, even the man in charge.

What Amorim said about wanting his side to fear losing was particularly poignant. In his time at the club so far he has repeatedly stressed that feeling of responsibility to honour the red and black shirt and all that comes with that, including the importance of results.

Some may argue that encouraging an ‘end of the world’ type mentality will not help the players play more carefree and will actually only stiffen them up. Yet, it could also provide the stimulus for the fight and the courage that Amorim clearly so desperately wants.

There is a hint of irony about the ‘no days off’ comment, as Amorim has given the squad a one-week break, at least those who were not called up by their national teams. When everyone reconvenes there will be another crucial stretch of games to see out the year, starting with a home match against the surprise package Frosinone.

For all of the energy, passion and emotion that Ruben Amorim speaks with, it will eventually be time for words to become deeds. Consistency must be not a distant mirage but some thing tangible that emerges.

Only then will a full buy-in be achieved and patience be awarded. Otherwise there will always be the fear that darkness follows light.

#2061. £8m Southampton outcast should be 'incredibly ambitious' Charlton Athletic transfer target

Charlton Athletic have been told to target Southampton’s Tom Fellows as they look to strengthen their squad in the January window.

It has been a crazy season so far for the Addicks, who followed up a brilliant start to the campaign with an 11-game winless run.

However, a 2-1 victory over Sheffield United means the Londoners went into the international break on a high, and whilst they are 17th in the table, they do have a seven-point advantage over the relegation zone.

Nevertheless, it’s clear that Jones’ squad is lacking in certain departments, and the January window will provide an opportunity for the boss to add quality.

However, the January window is notoriously difficult, and with Charlton not working with the biggest budget in the division, they will have to be smart with how they recruit.

And, when asked by FLW about one player the Addicks should try to bring in, Charlton fan pundit Chris Woodward explained why he feels the club should pursue a loan move for Southampton’s Tom Fellows, as he compared it to a previous deal involving James Bree that worked for all parties.

“We haven’t exactly got the budget to splash the cash. I think we’re limited in the quality moves we can make, especially in an inflated window. Therefore, I think we will have to look to the loan market," Chris told FLW.

“One position we lack right now is a natural right winger, and the squad in general is lacking creativity. It’s incredibly ambitious, but I’d look to try and take Tom Fellows on loan, as he ticks both boxes.

“It seems silly to suggest, but 12 months ago we had James Bree on loan, and now he is one of the best full-backs in the league!

“Fellows is out of form and out of favour at Southampton, and he’s not exactly loved by the fans at the moment. So he needs to build his confidence back up and get back to the player he was.

Find out which Championship team takes top spot for the highest house prices around their stadium from 2026 figures.

“Fellows is above Charlton’s level, but he may look at it as a chance to be a key player in a team where he would get a lot of the focus, and Southampton may look at the work we did with Bree, and some of our previous loans, and see how we turned them around. It's an ambitious signing, but it would be an incredible one.”

This may seem like a bold move, but the reality is that Fellows is enduring a difficult period right now, and he is not getting the game time he would’ve wanted a year on from his initial £8 million move from West Brom.

You can understand why Tonda Eckert is playing Kuryu Matsuki, as he is doing very well right now, but Fellows still isn’t getting the minutes he would’ve wanted, as he has been an unused sub in five of the last seven games.

At 23, Fellows is at a stage in his career where he needs to be playing regularly, and Southampton will know that they risk stalling his career if he stays on the bench.

So, if they can bring in a winger during the window themselves, a loan shouldn’t be ruled out for Fellows. And, as mentioned, the way Charlton helped Bree would give them a shot at making this happen if Fellows was available.

Most would agree that Charlton do need attacking additions in January as the lack of creativity and goals was a major problem in their poor run prior to the Blades win.

There was a reliance on Tyreece Campbell earlier in the campaign, and he was always going to struggle to sustain the numbers he was producing at that stage.

As well as his goals, Campbell is one of few players in the squad with genuine pace, so, even if they can’t get Fellows, he is the profile that they need to try and get in January.

Which player would you realistically like Charlton to sign in January? Let us know in the comments below.

Jones and the recruitment team have shown they have an eye for a player over the years, so it will be interesting to see who they do bring in, even if there’s a lot of football to be played before the window opens.

#2060. Tom Cannon in, George Hirst out: How Stoke City's dream January transfer window looks?

Stoke City are dreaming of a return to the Premier League once again after an excellent start to the 2026/27 campaign, and if Mark Robins' side can maintain this level of form for the next couple of months, the January transfer window becomes crucial to their efforts.

Stoke are flying right now in the Championship, sitting level on points with Birmingham City and Middlesbrough in 1st and 2nd, and narrowly ahead of West Bromwich Albion and Wolverhampton Wanderers in 4th and 5th, respectively.

The Potters, after three defeats on the spin to open the season against Swansea City, Southampton, and Wolverhampton, have followed that up with just one defeat in their following 12, winning nine.

If Mark Robins' side can maintain this level of form into the new year, the January window presents an opportunity to go all out and do what they can to secure promotion, as Football League World takes a look at what a dream window in the Potteries may look like.

Football League World has asked AI to rank the top nine toughest fanbases in the EFL Championship right now from least to most

Stoke have four different options they could start up front right now, namely George Hirst, Robert Bozenik, Lamine Cisse, and Sam Gallagher, though none of them has really been able to nail down a spot in the starting XI this campaign.

Hirst arrived in the summer from Ipswich Town for a potential £10 million, and with just one goal and one assist in 14 Championship appearances thus far, he failed to justify that fee.

Cisse enjoyed a run of games in the side between mid-September and mid-October, but injury has meant that Bozenik has been preferred up top as of late, whilst Gallagher also recovers from a fresh injury.

Despite this bloated list of strikers, there have been cries for another option up top from Stoke supporters as of late, with Sheffield United's Tom Cannon a name that is well-known in the Potteries.

Cannon, 23, scored 11 times in 25 appearances across all competitions on loan for Stoke from Leicester City during the first half of the 2024/25 campaign, before subsequently joining Sheffield United in January 2025 for around £10 million.

Things have not quite worked out at Bramall Lane for Cannon just yet, and given his popularity at the bet365 Stadium, he would be a dream addition for many supporters; whether a deal is likely, however, is doubtful.

If Cannon were to arrive, it would surely mean that one of their current strike force must depart, and following his lack of impact since his arrival, Hirst would likely be many fans' option to make way.

The former Leicester and Blackburn Rovers striker has never been prolific in his career, hitting double digits in goals in a season just twice at 27, despite earning three promotions with Ipswich under Kieran McKenna.

Whilst it is unlikely Hirst will be going anywhere anytime soon, his failure to justify his hefty fee, as well as Stoke supporters' preference for Cisse, Bozenik, and Gallagher, make him the ideal player to depart.

In reality, one of Bozenik or Gallagher is more likely to leave in January; with the latter's contract due to expire in the summer and now aged 31, it's doubtful he will be offered fresh terms, especially with a subpar injury record.

What would be your dream January window, Stoke fans? Who would you like to see join, and who would you like to see depart? Share your thoughts below!

There are numerous players, as a result of Stoke's summer recruitment, that have been pushed out to the fringes of the squad, as the likes of Bae Jun-ho, Million Manhoef, Tomas Rigo, Ben Pearson, and Ben Gibson have seen their minutes slashed.

Jun-ho, 23, is due to enter the final 12 months of his deal in North Staffordshire, and at this stage, a fresh deal appears incredibly unlikely, as the emergence of Justin Devenny and Jack McGlynn has seen the Korean's game time dwindle.

Ben Pearson has managed just 14 minutes of Championship football this season, with Ethan Galbraith, Djibril Soumare, and Svante Ingelsson's arrivals knocking the midfielder down the pecking order.

Manhoef, Rigo, and Gibson have all barely featured as well, though the most likely to leave in the winter are surely Jun-ho and Pearson, as time will tell how Stoke's season unfolds.
