#1950. “Cashing in” on Castellanos claim ignores one major stumbling block | West Ham News

Ever since the closing days of the summer transfer window there have been claims that West Ham will be cashing in on Taty Castellanos in the winter: The Argentine has been a huge disappointment in the 15 games of West Ham’s championship season, with just a solitary goal to show for his efforts.

At times he’s resembled more of a moody, disinterested bystander and seems pretty much the most likely player in the eleven to be yellow carded each time he plays.

A solitary goal is plain unacceptable for the frontman who cost £27 million: Claims that he’ll be sold in the winter abound.

Sadly, Everton’s late interest in the summer window, reportedly around £40 million, appears to have evaporated as Taty’s form has waned. Understandably.

Far from happy: One goal in fifteen means Castellanos has been a huge let down in the second tier. Its also means those big money suitors have now evaporated

The newest suggestions from EFL specialist site the72.co.uk suggest Castellanos could be heading back home – however there’s a catch:

“River Plate reportedly view the 28-year-old as a priority target in their striker search, although the finances involved in the deal could prove to be a major hurdle. However, cashing in could give WHUFC the chance to sign a true talisman to aid their promotion bid. “

“Cashing in”? I think not: That’s the elephant in the room here. River Plate have already disclosed that they’ll look at some kind of loan or shared purchase option – as they’re short of funds – which of course will cut no ice with West Ham who will want to replace Taty with a striker more suited to scoring the Championship goals they require.

Merely shipping Taty out on loan without a permanent sale will serve no useful purpose and could actually weaken Scott Parker’s squad. The Hammers have enough loaned – out unwanted stars as it is: Another one added to the list won’t help a rebuild. The only possible route could involve a swap for goal keeper Santiago Beltran – which would still leave the Hammers short of a goal scorer and needing to offload Hermansen or Areola in the winter.

And how often to these player swaps ever come off? Exactly.

#1948. Steven Gerrard explains his theory on why Alexis Mac Allister has been so resurgent this season

Steven Gerrard has offered a theory as to why Alexis Mac Allister has looked so resurgent this season compared to last.

The midfielder was one of the Reds’ most disappinting players of a dreadful 2025/26 campaign, especially having been such a key component in the preceding Premier League title triumph, but he’s been playing near to his best since Andoni Iraola took charge in the summer.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily (via Liverpool Echo), our former captain claimed that the 27-year-old subconsciously let his performance levels drop last season as he was privately consumed by trying to retain the World Cup with Argentina.

Gerrard said of Mac Allister: “I’ve loved him this season. I think last year, like a lot of the Argentinian players, they had a bit of a distraction with the World Cup coming up.

“It’s the way they are. The World Cup takes over everything in their lives, and I lived that with Emiliano Martínez when I was at Aston Villa. I just think it becomes a priority.

“I think it becomes a bit of a distraction. It becomes the most important thing in their lives, to be ready and not injured and make sure that the national team is the priority.

“I think with a lot of the Argentina players, I’m sure a lot of managers, if they watch this, will say: ‘Yeah, I’ve experienced that.’”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

It’s an interesting theory that Gerrard has put forward to explain why Mac Allister’s performances from last season to this have been so chalk and cheese.

Many footballers consider the World Cup as the pinnacle of their careers, and the Liverpool midfielder represents a nation where the sport is nothing short of an obsession.

Only the 27-year-old could truthfully answer whether or not he let his levels dip in 2025/26 because he was prioritising the global tournament in North America, but from a Reds perspective we’d hope that isn’t the case.

As a player employed by LFC, Mac Allister has a duty to give full commitment to representing the club. As disappointing as his performances were last season, though, we wouldn’t go as far as accusing him of not giving less than 100%, which’d be a serious indictment of an elite footballer.

Thankfully, the Argentine has looked much more like his usual self since August, to the point where Troy Deeney suggested that he would even inspire Liverpool to nudge their way into the Premier League title race if he maintains or improves further upon his current standards.

The 27-year-old has been vocal about his contract situation at Anfield, but if he keeps playing the way that he has been, securing a new deal for him should become a matter of priority for sporting director Richard Hughes.

The biggest single factor on which most West Ham supporters agree is the choice of goalkeeper. According to the survey:

“Of the fans surveyed, an overwhelming 85.4 per cent believe Alphonse Areola should reclaim the No 1 jersey from Mads Hermansen.

Likeable yes, dependable no: 85% of West Ham fans want Hermansen out of the team

Interestingly, though, a sizeable 62 per cent of supporters believe the travelling contingent at Ewood Park were not right to boo Hermansen.”

Eighty five percent of fans have had enough of the Dane’s inept performances in between the sticks, with one fan driven to comment that West Ham’s goal would be better defended simply by hanging a green jersey on the cross bar rather than continuing to select the out of form Hermansen.

Of course the fly in the ointment is that Areola has been reported as ‘unfit’ – whether that means third choice Finlay Herrick comes into consideration – who can say- but it’d be a brave selection for Parker to leave his number one on the bench if Areola isn’t ready for the Preston North End fixture next weekend, however much it seems supporters want to see Hermansen out of the team.

Alphadjo Cisse is the man of the moment for AC Milan, and yet there were some within the club at the time who opposed his arrival.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

There is now talk of Premier League clubs expressing their interest in signing him, but in the meantime Milan have a counter-move ready: the extension of his contract with a pay rise as a reward.

MilanNews reveal the back story regarding his arrival. In January, Cisse seemed destined to join PSV Eindhoven, but a phone call from Milan changed everything. When the Rossoneri entered the race, the forward put PSV on hold and made it clear where he wanted to go.

Milan then convinced Verona with a bid of €8m and persuaded Cisse with a development plan, including that he could remain on loan in Serie B with Catanzaro. Geoffrey Moncada identified him and Giorgio Furlani was key in the negotiations with his agency CAA Base, too.

However, not everyone at Milan was in favour. The report claims that Massimiliano Allegri did not like the idea of allocating part of the budget on a young player while his side were in a title fight. Niclas Füllkrug was the only first-team reinforcement, arriving on loan from West Ham.

Allegri did not fail to express his ‘annoyance and negativity’ regarding the Cisse operation, which was later finalised by Furlani. In the end, the head coach, CEO and the chief scout (Moncada) would all be dismissed after the final game of the season.

#1942. Chaos appears to be following one West Ham want away as upheaval continues

There’s been another twist in the chaotic career of one of West Ham’s standout signings of the Tim Steidten era.

It would be fair to say that Jean Clair Todibo was largely unknown to Hammers fans when Tim Stediten whisked the former Barca defender to east London in his private jet for a VIP welcome in the summer of 2024.

Sadly its would also be fair to say that the defender has been part of a chaotic two and a half years during which he’s seen three West Ham managers – and fallen out with all of them – and declared himself unwilling to play for the club again.

Todibo – dressing room chaos never seems far away

Chaos appears to have followed Todibo to France when West Ham finally – gratefully – found a loan destination for their unhappy defender in the summer as Todibo was sent to Lens owing to his desire (apparently) to work with manager Dino Toppmoller.

No sooner had the wayward West Ham defender landed than Toppmoller was fired – and his successor Yannick Cahuzac fared little better, lasting just two months.

Todibo is surely the only player in the Lens dressing room who will have played under six managers in side three years, as his new head coach is revealed as Didier Digard.

#1940. Championship data highlights exactly what West Ham’s midfield is still missing

A fascinating piece of Championship analysis from Loft Insights on X may provide an uncomfortable reminder of where West Ham’s midfield falls short.

The graphic plots central midfielders based on two key metrics: line-breaking passes per 90 minutes and ball-winning actions per 90 minutes. Put simply, it measures which players are able to progress the ball through opposition lines while also contributing defensively.

The most interesting takeaway for me was not necessarily which players stand out, but where West Ham’s own midfield profiles sit on the chart.

The Championship’s elite midfielders increasingly occupy the top-right quadrant, combining progression and defensive intensity. That is why the chart identifies Norwich City’s Kenny McLean as one of the Championship’s most complete midfielders, posting outstanding line-breaking numbers while maintaining strong defensive output, despite only featuring for ten games out of fifteen due to an ankle injury.

Meanwhile, Portsmouth’s Ebou Adams is highlighted as a “defensive monster”, producing exceptional ball-winning statistics while still offering significant progression. Sheffield United’s Kalvin Phillips (yes the same player that flopped on loan at West Ham!), Queens Park Rangers’ Jonathan Varane and Norwich’s Jacob Wright also occupy impressive positions, demonstrating the ability to impact both sides of the game.

Mohamadou Kanté is viewed as a dynamic ball-carrying midfielder with strong physical attributes, but his game is built more around energy and transition play than elite progression metrics. Arne Engels offers technical quality and creativity, yet is generally more comfortable operating higher up the pitch than acting as a defensive controller.

The data is only based on players who have played an average of 540 mins so one omission is Tomas Souček, whose strengths have always been obvious. The Czech international on paper would arguably be the Championships most effective midfield goalscorer (3 in 7 appearances so far) and I’d expect him to feature highly for aerial presence. However, if plotted on a graph measuring line-breaking passes and ball-winning volume, he would likely owe more to his physicality and attacking threat than his ability to dictate possession through midfield.

That perhaps explains why West Ham can sometimes appear disconnected between defence and attack.

Too often there is a reliance on direct balls into attacking areas rather than building through the centre of the pitch. Equally, when possession is lost, the midfield does not always possess the combination of mobility and defensive output needed to regain control quickly.

West Ham arguably have midfielders who can create and win duels. What they appear to lack is a genuine “two-way” midfielder capable of consistently ranking highly in both categories.

That was precisely what Declan Rice offered during his time at the club. His ability to recover possession and immediately progress the ball remains incredibly difficult to replace.

The reality is Rice was never truly replaced, although finding a like-for-like successor was always going to be a near-impossible task

Former West Ham midfielder James Ward-Prowse’s position on the chart is also interesting. A casualty of Nuno’s reign, he ranks among the highest players for line-breaking passes but has one of the lowest ball-winning outputs. Ward-Prowse excels at progressing possession but offers relatively little defensive contribution compared to the league’s most complete midfielders.

Above all the data serves as a reminder that Koppen’s recruitment and Parker’s existing choices for midfield should focus less on individual statistics and more on complete profiles.

Because the numbers suggest that is where Championship matches are increasingly won.

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

I think there is nothing wrong with the Midfield. There is just a problem with the short pass mentality. The day of playing short passes across midfield are over in English football. You need decent long passes with good trapping and decent positive movement. How many of West Ham’s passes are square ball or back passes ? Far to many. Particularly back passes are all to often caught on to giving away needless goals. Walker-Peters is a really good example. Having moved forward beating someone, he then passes back in midfield, or worst still carries the ball backwards towards midfield or defence. Play positively, avoid back passes, learn to pass well and trap well and you have a very good midfield. Orford, Kante and other young players are far better at doing this, than the older players.

#1939. “Make them excel and get better”- Returning hero’s stated West Ham ambition

Along with regime change and boardroom change this year, there has been evolution in the West Ham United coaching department as Nuno’s team departed along with  their Portuguese boss and Scott Parker brought in his own hand-picked replacements.

As we covered last week, alongside the headline hires, one of the lesser known appointments was for former West Ham hero – and son of hero – David Martin to rejoin West Ham’s coaching team as the Academy’s head of goal keeping.

David Martin’s West Ham career was short but never-to-be-forgotten

Martin has been quick to praise the talent available to him in his new role: Speaking to West Ham’s web site, the 40 year old confirmed his own methodical approach:

“I enjoy having a plan, making the very most of myself and my abilities, being a good person and making people around me better…

“That’s what the role is – creating a competitive environment where people can learn and improve under pressure. I’ve got two very good young goalkeepers in the development squad – Fin Hooper and Lanre Awesu – and it’s an unbelievable competition between them and I want that to make them excel and get better.”

Of course with former academy graduate Finlay Herrick now officially Scott Parker’s third choice keeper, (and not forgetting Mason Terry who is out on loan) the Hammers do have an embarrassment of riches in their ‘up and coming’ goal keeping department.

It can only be a matter of time before Herrick progresses – something tells me this might be sooner than we think – and it is good to see that West Ham are embracing their heritage with an appointment like Martin’s to a pivotal post within the club.

#1937. James Pearce claim seems to pour cold water over Liverpool links with Finn Jeltsch

Liverpool, it’s fair to say, have a pretty active recruiting department.

A necessarily active recruiting department, it should be emphasised, given the squad-building challenges Andoni Iraola has already faced early on in his tenure as head coach.

The Merseysiders navigated a potential centre-back crisis expertly in the summer with the arrival of loan signing Ronald Araujo from Barcelona. But questions remain as to the long-term viability of the centre-back department post the summer 2027 transfer window.

A recent report from Christian Falk with CF Bayern Insider asserted that Liverpool, among Europe’s elite, have scouted VfB Stuttgart centre-back Finn Jeltsch.

“It is TRUE: Liverpool have scouted VfB Stuttgart centre-back Finn Jeltsch. All the top clubs, including Bayern Munich, are scouting him,” the head of football at Bild said.

“He was in the squad for Klopp first as a backup for the right-back. Then one of the central defenders became injured, and now he’s also the backup at centre-back. This shows he can play many positions, and everyone can see the 20-year-old’s potential.

“Such players really are a present to everyone. Jeltsch is young, talented and can play many positions, and he’s not so expensive! Bayern Munich has an eye on him.”

If that name seems vaguely familiar, it might be because Bundesliga giants Bayern Munich are already big fans of the footballer and are keeping a very close eye on matters close to home.

Liverpool’s interest is understandable. Come the summer transfer window, they could be two centre-halves down should Joe Gomez and Virgil van Dijk call time on their Anfield careers once their contracts run out. Ronald Araujo, though enjoying an impeccable campaign with the Reds, may not become a permanent addition to the squad, despite Liverpool possessing a buy option. Much here may depend on what Barcelona’s stance on the Uruguayan international looks like in May.

That’s three centre-backs Liverpool could be short come the opening of the summer transfer window, so it’s very plausible that Julian Ward and Co. will be keeping a close eye on the centre-back market between now and the end of the 2026/27 season.

As James Pearce rightly notes on X (formerly Twitter), of course, Liverpool do have several high-potential, highly exciting young centre-backs in their stable.

Ifeanyi Ndukwe, by all accounts, is impressing on loan at Levante after an eye-catching pre-season; Giovanni Leoni remains an appetising option, and then there’s hope for young Mor Talla Ndiaye also.

Centre-back not a priority for Liverpool so highly unlikely they will invest heavily in that area either in Jan or next summer. Jacquet has made a huge impact and big hopes for fellow young CBs Leoni, Ndukwe and Ndiaye.

— James Pearce (@JamesPearceLFC) November 13, 2026

But these are three very young, very inexperienced centre-backs you’d be pairing with the also youthful, but extremely impressive, Jeremy Jacquet for the foreseeable future. The Frenchman will, however, have a season of Premier League football under his belt – but is that enough to help guide the next generation of Liverpool centre-backs?

Unless you’re planning to extend Van Dijk’s contract or activate Araujo’s buy option, Liverpool are looking incredibly short on options with experience and genuine leadership credentials at L4.

That might be worth considering if the plan isn’t to invest in Finn Jeltsch this summer.

#1936. West Ham Winger Faces Another Fitness Test As Parker Waits

West Ham United are facing something of a dilemma over Manor Solomon, with Israel reportedly considering bringing the winger back into the team for Tuesday’s Nations League clash against Austria. The 26-year-old has been struggling with back pain during the international break, although Israel manager Ran Ben-Shimon has suggested that he is feeling better after returning to training.

According to Sport5, Solomon could now be in contention for the Austria fixture. That follows comments from Ben-Shimon suggesting the player had trained and was feeling better, although his fitness would need to be reassessed.

For West Ham manager Scott Parker, however, the situation presents an interesting dilemma. We desperately need the old Manor Solomon back, but I wonder whether another international appearance is really what the player needs right now.

Manor Solomon representing Israel during a difficult international break. The West Ham winger has been carrying a back injury since October

Look, I’m caught between a rock and a hard place on this one.

There is part of me that hopes Solomon gets a game, so he can get back to form. Because there’s no doubt about it, West Ham have a far bigger chance of getting promoted this season if Manor Solomon is back to the sort of form he was in when he played for Leeds in the Championship.

Clearly Scott Parker has faith in him because he has seen how destructive he can be in that division. Getting that player back would be a significant boost for the Hammers, particularly with the Championship promotion race starting to get serious.

But, and it’s a big but, we have had complaints of back injury during the October internationals, and we’ve already had it during this international break.

As I reported earlier in October, a West Ham source confirmed that Solomon was in considerable pain after an exhausting international schedule. More recently, we reported on his latest back problem, which restricted his training with Israel.

There is also part of me that wonders whether we would not have been better served, and the player himself, actually resting up, getting some medical treatment, or even being given ten days off completely to recuperate and joining back up with the squad for the last few days of training before the Preston game.

As things stand, there’s nothing in his recent form that suggests he could start and should start against Preston. And without him being on the training pitch during this international break to impress Scott Parker, he’s not going to be able to catch the manager’s eye.

Edvin Austbø has certainly given Parker something to think about on the left wing. Indeed, Austbø’s recent performances have highlighted the competition for Solomon’s place, and I suspect the Norwegian is currently ahead of him in the pecking order.

But I don’t want to write off Solomon. We know what he’s capable of producing in this division, and West Ham will need every bit of attacking quality available if we’re serious about getting back into the Premier League.

Hopefully, Israel will make the sensible decision and only involve him against Austria if he is genuinely fit enough to play. We cannot afford another international break to leave us with a player who returns to east London carrying another injury.

Pio Esposito, Lulli, Mora (the three who have always won as starters), Zaccagni, Dimarco, Isaksen, and Zielinski rank higher, but there’s a clear difference: the others play for Lazio, Inter, and Roma, the top three in the league.

Captain America came on against Benfica, Bologna, and Ferencvaros, and was an unused substitute against Bournemouth. Compared to Modric, who has been playing consistently since August, and Gila, who has been affected by injury, Pulisic has had his ups and downs.

He scored in Udine, the derby and most recently against Genoa, and it’s no coincidence that the Diavolo won all three games. Simply put: when Christian plays well, Milan follow him. When his level drops, Milan struggle.

It’s tactics, as well as numbers. Pulisic has different characteristics from his team-mates: he’s the only one who attacks the space in behind. Gonçalo Ramos often comes deep and lays it off, Alphadjo Cisse loves having the ball at his feet, and CP disrupts defences in other ways.

Furthermore, he’s considered one of the owners’ key players, who are also American, and he just renewed his contract. If you have to imagine the Milan of the future, just think Pulisic and 10 others.

#1930. Liverpool tipped for January squad boost absolutely no one wants

Harvey Elliott is reportedly set to be sent packing back home to Liverpool in January.

That’s the claim coming out of the regional Valencian outlet Las Provincias (via Sport Witness), with the midfielder having only picked up 152 La Liga minutes out of a possible 810 on offer.

After some concerns were expressed over the former Fulham academy graduate having arrived overweight in the Spanish top-flight, it seems the 23-year-old has been unable to make any headway at Mestalla.

It’s worth noting that a permanent decision has yet to be made by the club, despite a string of concerns, but Elliott very much appears to be in the last-chance saloon. In fact, as relayed by Sport Witness: “If he does not improve in the coming weeks, the loan agreement with Liverpool could be terminated. They state that ‘talks will be held’.”

Not a lot of time for the footballer to buck up his ideas and earn himself a place in the hearts of the Valencia fans and, importantly, the decision-makers at the outfit.

It’s not looking great for Harvey Elliott, it has to be said.

After basically being iced out of the Liverpool squad by former Reds head coach Andoni Iraola, the playmaker was shipped off to Unai Emery’s Aston Villa and only picked up 284 minutes of action.

Mind, there seemed to be a weird kind of power play going on between Liverpool and the Villans, with the Reds unwilling to pay a significant amount of cash to cut the loan short and Emery’s side being apparently fine with letting a young player rot on the bench to make a point.

Point made. And now Elliott’s future is paying for it.

We do want to state, unequivocally, that we believe in Harvey Elliott and his potential. It wasn’t a million years ago when we were watching him thriving as part of Jurgen Klopp’s deep squad in the German’s final season in charge in 2023/24. But that season is becoming increasingly distant, and it’s becoming increasingly difficult to imagine Elliott ever playing a significant role for Liverpool again in future.

We hope he can turn things around in Valencia. Because if our No.19 comes back to L4 in January, it’s not an eventuality that will suit the player or the club at this stage.

Ian Rush has disagreed with the common consensus about Alexander Isak this season.

But the fact remains that Isak is managing to get on the scoresheet with some degree of frequency as part of a frontline that is far from cohesive at this stage.

One may reasonably be inclined to think that critics have forgotten how Isak had the debut season from hell at Liverpool following his move from Newcastle in the summer.

The forward managed only 1,032 minutes across all competitions in Arne Slot’s final season in charge, between adductor issues and a broken fibula. 1,032 minutes, four goals and one assist. In 2026/27, the Swede has already racked up eight goals and an assist in 899 minutes of action (across all competitions).

Far easier for Alexander Isak to build fluency when he’s spending a lot more time on the pitch early in the season and stringing a series of starts together from one game to the next.

#1926. ‘I felt my leg…’ – Dominik Szoboszlai makes worrying injury admission after Hungary win

Dominik Szoboszlai has given an update on his knee injury after Hungary’s win over Georgia on Saturday, and his comments could be quite concerning for Liverpool fans.

The midfielder’s involvement for his country during this international window was placed in doubt after the knock that he incurred in the Reds’ victory at Crystal Palace last weekend, although he still linked up with Marco Rossi’s squad for their UEFA Nations League fixtures.

The Hungarian FA had deferred any decision on whether the 26-year-old would play until the last minute, but he featured for the entirety of his nation’s 2-0 triumph in Tbilisi and claimed the assist for Barnabas Varga’s clinching goal.

Szoboszlai revealed after the match that he nearly pulled out of playing after he felt a twinge during the warm-up prior to kick-off, but his determination to feature would eventually prevail.

In quotes relayed by Nemzeti Sport, the Hungary captain said: “I was always 100% sure that I would be able to play, but the doctors were less sure. I progressed day by day, focused on myself, received treatment.

“I played with my leg for a training session and a half, and in the warm-up I was close to cancelling it because I felt my leg on one of the shots, but if I’ve come this far, I won’t let the team down. Now the treatment starts all over again. I have to be ready again by Tuesday.”

Szoboszlai’s comments may well come as a worry to Liverpool fans, with the midfielder admitting that he played through the pain barrier and seemingly defied the assessment of medical professionals.

It’s natural that, as captain of his country, the Reds’ number 8 will stop at nothing to try and be available for them, but his club will be left praying that he comes through the Magyars’ next game unscathed.

Szoboszlai will return from international duty into a hectic run of 11 Liverpool fixtures before the end of December, and we’ll need him and his teammates to be operating at their best throughout that busy period.

#1925. 20 Most Beautiful Wives and Girlfriends (WAGs) in World Soccer Ranked

Correspondent AUTHORITY Football journalist with experience at Reach PLC and PA Media; University of Central Lancashire graduate. FOCUS Fan-engagement content and match analysis across the Premier League and Championship. THE INSIGHT Oliver utilises a network of club and industry contacts to deliver verified reporting and fan-first content. He provides the human stories behind the results to ensure fans get the full picture as it happens.

From red-carpet galas to World Cup stands, the wives and girlfriends of soccer’s biggest icons command nearly as much global attention as the superstars on the pitch.

Originally coined by the British press during the 2006 World Cup, the term "WAG" has evolved into a worldwide pop-culture phenomenon—defined by power couples, luxury fashion, and massive social media empires.

Today, the partners of the game's biggest stars are household names in their own right, blending chart-topping careers, modeling contracts, and business ventures with life alongside football royalty.

Football Insider has ranked the 20 most beautiful and iconic wives and girlfriends in world soccer—spanning both current stars and retired legends—based on global star power, glamour, and cultural impact.

Scroll down to see who claims the number one spot, and let us know in the comments who we ranked too low.

Brazilian supermodel Goulart began dating German goalkeeper Trapp in 2015, with the pair getting engaged in July 2018. She is best known for her work as a Victoria's Secret Angel from 2005 to 2008, and for walking in the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show from 2005 through 2016. She has also modelled for leading designers and luxury brands, including Armani, Chanel and Valentino, while appearing on numerous covers of major fashion magazines.

Renowned for her athletic physique and natural elegance, 42-year-old Goulart is widely regarded as one of the most beautiful women in the modelling industry. She boasts over four million followers on Instagram.

Ivanovic is a star in her own right, after spending over a decade as one of the leading women's tennis players from 2003 to her retirement in 2016. She reached the number one spot for 12 weeks in 2008 and won an impressive 15 singles career titles, including the 2008 French Open.

The Serbian began a relationship with former Bayern Munich and Man United star Schweinsteiger in 2014, and they married in Venice in 2016. The pair had three children in the next seven years but decided to end their marriage in 2025.

Johansen is one of the biggest names of the latest era of WAGs, owing to the meteoric rise to stardom of her partner, Haaland, over the last decade. She was a soccer player who came through the youth ranks of his boyhood club, Bryne FK, and the pair knew each other from childhood before beginning a relationship in 2021.

The couple have kept details of their relationship remarkably private, considering his fame, but 22-year-old Johansen has amassed a huge Instagram following of over two million followers and is now considered a celebrity in their home country of Norway. She has adorned the cover of numerous high-profile national magazines, and the couple have one son together.

Hertfordshire native Benson is another relatively new face of WAG culture, becoming one of the standout figures of this era thanks to her striking looks and impeccable style. She drew national attention in 2024 after being photographed in the stands watching England star partner Saka at that summer's Euros.

She has built a career of her own, working in media planning and communications after studying Public Relations and Media at Birmingham City University. She reportedly met the Arsenal winger in 2020, and the couple announced their engagement in November 2025 to huge fanfare online. Adoring followers are waiting with bated breath for details and photos of whenever they do tie the knot soon.

Rubio has enjoyed a substantial career in Spanish entertainment independent of her relationship with Real Madrid legend Ramos. She appeared on numerous comedy programmes in their home country in the 1990s and 2000s, then started to present game shows and appear in movies as her profile grew outside of Spain.

Rubio was named Spain's sexiest woman by FHM magazine in both 2008 and 2009, and began dating Ramos in 2012. They are now known as one of the most iconic couples in soccer history, as they have since married and share four sons. Rubio is still active as a TV presenter and boasts a whopping 10.6m followers on Instagram.

Nara and Icardi's story is one that has dominated news headlines far and wide for many years. It is perhaps the most publicised soccer romance of the last decade. The Argentine television personality is widely known for her glamorous appearance and confident personality, but the relationship has made her a globally known star.

She was initially married to Icardi's Sampdoria teammate and friend, Maxi Lopez, but they separated in late 2013 and by May 2014 Nara was controversially married to the Argentine international. The players' games against each other were subsequently known as the 'Wanda Derby'. They were then involved in a major scandal in 2021, as Nara accused Icardi of being unfaithful, and despite several reconciliation attempts and children involved, they were officially divorced in October 2026.

Carbonero is one of Spain's most recognisable media personalities, admired for her effortless elegance and long-standing body of journalistic work. She rose to prominence covering football for La Sexta and Telecinco in the noughties and first met legendary goalkeeper Casillas while they were both working at the 2009 Confederations Cup.

Their relationship became known across the globe due to a surprise embrace live on air at the 2010 World Cup after Spain's victory in the final while she interviewed her partner. The couple wed in 2016 and built a family, but separated in 2021.

Vinicius' status as a global superstar in soccer has been flanked by his on-off relationship with Fonseca over the last 18 months, which has unsurprisingly kept them both in the headlines for both good and bad reasons. The USA-born influencer moved to Brazil as a child and became immensely famous for her YouTube channel and previous relationships with notable media and music personalities before meeting the Madrid forward in 2025.

She attended his 25th birthday in July as they grew closer, and the pair confirmed a relationship later that year. They split in May 2026 as Fonseca alluded to their differences online, but reconciled two months later before separating again in October. She remains one of Brazil’s most influential internet personalities, keeping her huge 57m Instagram following updated with snapshots into the glamorous life she is currently leading without Vinicius by her side.

Bellingham is one of the biggest stars in soccer right now, and his enormous commercial appeal has inevitably led to intrigue around his personal life. He has been romantically linked to American model Castro since 2024 after they reportedly matched on celebrity dating app Raya.

The California-born personality is actually six years older than her English superstar boyfriend, and became known before their relationship for her budding modelling career and appearances in music videos for globally known artists like Drake and DJ Khaled. She is regularly spotted at his games for club and country and has developed a sizeable social media following as a result of their romance.

Sabatini is another who can count herself as a celebrity in her own right without Argentine international husband Dybala to boost her profile. She hails from a family of actors and sportspeople, and was a child actor who won awards for her work on nationally acclaimed TV show Aliados.

She opened live shows for the likes of Ariana Grande and Coldplay after turning her attention to music in 2017, and met Dybala at a concert of the former. The pair married in 2024 and have since started a family. Sabatini boasts over 68m streams as a music artist on Spotify.

Stunning blonde Ward always seemed destined for fame in some measure, after her mother, Dawn, became a multi-millionaire through interior design and her father, Ashley, had his own soccer career in the Premier League. Dawn shot to fame on The Real Housewives of Cheshire in 2015 and Taylor appeared on the show while building her own profile as a model and fashion influencer online.

She met Algerian star Mahrez through a mutual friend in 2020, and they quickly became a real power couple as English media lapped up the idea of two very different worlds colliding through fame. They appeared together on Amazon Prime’s 2024 documentary series Married to the Game, and are now married and have children.

Pinnock is a very clear example of a modern-day WAG who is actually much more famous than her soccer-playing partner. The striking chart-topping pop star is one of Britain’s most recognisable celebrities after forming one quarter of the hugely successful girl group Little Mix between 2010 and 2021. The X Factor-formed collective sold more than 50m records worldwide and boasted five UK number one singles.

She met former Burnley and Watford striker Gray while holidaying in Marbella in 2016, as they soon got together and were eventually married in Jamaica in 2023. Pinnock is currently pursuing a solo music career and is branching out into the world of TV and fashion.

Pinnock’s former bandmate and close friend Edwards has also found herself in the WAG world for a similar length of time. The cheeky Geordie shared the highs of Little Mix’s extraordinary success after initially applying to The X Factor as a solo contestant.

Edwards met Celtic midfielder Oxlade-Chamberlain on Raya in 2016, and they made their first public appearance at the 2017 BRIT Awards to massive excitement and media attention. They were engaged in 2022 and welcomed two children before tying the knot after almost 10 years together in June 2026. With Little Mix on an indefinite hiatus, her debut solo album ‘Perrie’ reached number three in the UK charts in September 2025.

The idea of a soccer WAG first became a prominent part of British culture and the wider celebrity world during the 2006 World Cup in Germany. English international star Rooney had been with his future wife, Coleen, for a decade, and she was arguably the most important figure in the early era of the WAG in soccer, becoming one of the most recognisable faces among Three Lions’ players’ partners at the tournament.

She was launched to stardom alongside him as a teenager in the early noughties, with tabloids watching their every move and the Liverpool native developing her own career through high-profile endorsements and TV appearances. She is still as big a name as ever, despite his retirement, and has retained a down-to-earth image that many can relate to, especially after the huge 2019 ‘Wagatha Christie’ scandal.

Clancy is widely known for her slender figure and glamorous looks which have seen her dominate the WAG world for decades on end. She finished as runner-up on Britain’s Next Top Model in 2006 and was instantly propelled into an international career in the industry that saw her adorn the covers of numerous iconic fashion magazines and amass huge wealth in her own right.

The former Strictly Come Dancing winner met England hero Crouch in 2006 shortly after he had signed for Liverpool, as they began dating, were engaged in 2009 and wed in 2011. She has continued to keep up national celebrity status with appearances on red carpets galore, high-profile modelling contracts and increased TV appearances. She is also renowned for her down-to-earth persona and sense of humour, a popular match for the man who popularised the 'Robot' dance during his cult-hero playing days.

Neymar is a modern-day Brazilian icon who has dominated social media and the wider sporting zeitgeist of the last 15 years, and so his romance with Biancardi has also attracted major interest across the globe. She was a known Instagram and YouTube influencer before their relationship, but was catapulted to worldwide fame when they went public online in 2022.

Their turbulent partnership has been closely scrutinised since then, with allegations of infidelity and subsequent reunions in abundance, which have all been played out in front of a widespread online audience. Biancardi now has more than 15m followers on Instagram and shares three children with the Selecao soccer star.

Shakira needs little introduction as a global superstar and a phenomenon of Latin pop music who is among the world’s best-selling artists of all time. She is credited with popularising Spanish-language music across the globe and has carved out her own path as a soccer icon with her 2010 World Cup anthem ‘Waka Waka’ and 2026 official song ‘Dai Dai.’

Her romance with ex-Barcelona and Spain defender Pique was one of the most high-profile in sports history, and actually began at the 2010 tournament. They became a prominent celebrity couple who were followed everywhere by paparazzi, and even shared two children, but made particular headlines after a bitter 2022 split that later saw the Colombian star aim a diss track at her ex-partner.

Another global superstar music artist makes the top three of our list, with ‘Posh Spice’ Beckham still known as the benchmark against which WAG style is measured. They were the original soccer celebrity couple who transcended the sport after building hugely successful and high profile respective careers in their own domains.

Victoria has evolved from cultural pop icon to one of the biggest fashion designers on the planet in the 21st century, with the pair still by each other’s side to this day after first dating in 1997 (albeit while surviving a dose or two of scandal along the way). She is also a mother of four who remains heavily involved with several of the biggest fashion labels in the world, and boasts a massive online presence to boot. The original but, on our list, not quite the best.

Roccuzzo and Messi share a love story that has stood the test of time. Being the childhood sweetheart of the greatest soccer player ever can’t have always been easy, but the sweet Rosario native has stuck by his side and tried to remain as out of the public eye as possible throughout his decorated career. She moved to Barcelona to be with him in 2010, and they wed in 2017.

Her public profile is low-key but active, as she cares for their three children and keeps her 42m Instagram followers regularly updated with a glimpse into the lifestyle of one of the most famous sporting families ever. Roccuzzo also utilises her following to front commercial campaigns for global companies like Adidas, DoorDash and Anastasia Beverley Hills.

The world’s biggest sports star needs a strong partner by his side, and Ronaldo has had Spanish glamour model Rodriguez on his arm for over 10 years now. She has embraced global stardom and built a successful career on top of her relationship to become an icon of modern celebrity culture as an individual.

Rodriguez boasts the most Instagram followers of any WAG on this list by some margin, at over 77m, regularly works with top fashion brands and is often seen at the biggest events in fashion, film and television. She was the subject of Netflix docuseries ‘I Am Georgina’ between 2022 and 2024, and remains a figure of constant fascination, with swathes of adoring fans hanging on her every move.

#1923. 20 Richest Soccer Players of All Time Ranked by Net Worth

Correspondent AUTHORITY Football journalist with experience at Reach PLC and PA Media; University of Central Lancashire graduate. FOCUS Fan-engagement content and match analysis across the Premier League and Championship. THE INSIGHT Oliver utilises a network of club and industry contacts to deliver verified reporting and fan-first content. He provides the human stories behind the results to ensure fans get the full picture as it happens.

Massive salaries, lifetime shoe deals, and global business empires have turned soccer’s biggest icons into some of the wealthiest athletes on earth.

Today, iconic figures like David Beckham earn hundreds of millions off the pitch through club ownership, fashion ventures, and brand partnerships that even dwarf their mega on-pitch earnings.

From record-breaking contracts in Saudi Arabia and Major League Soccer to royal family fortunes like Faiq Bolkiah’s, the financial scale of modern soccer is staggering.

Football Insider has ranked the 20 richest soccer players of all time by estimated net worth, combining career wages, endorsement deals, and post-playing investments.

Scroll down to see who tops the rich list, and let us know in the comments which fortune surprises you most. There are some huge shocks that nobody would have expected.

Pep Guardiola has reshaped modern soccer more profoundly than any other figure of his generation, turning his tactical blueprint into global celebrity and a £100m ($132.3m) fortune. While the Spaniard enjoyed a decorated playing career with Barcelona and Spain, the vast majority of his wealth has been built from the touchline through record-breaking managerial contracts at Barcelona, Bayern Munich, and Manchester City.

The Spaniard was believed to be earning around £35m ($46.3m) annually, with bonuses included, during his final years in charge of Man City. He owns high-value property in England and his home country, and has partnered with the likes of Puma, Nissan and Visa to bolster his whopping fortune over the years.

Ultra-passionate Atletico Madrid manager Simeone is widely regarded as the highest-paid in his profession right now, owing to how desperate the La Liga club are to hold onto his services for as long as humanly possible. Some reports estimate that he takes home around £26m ($34.4m) each year as they aim to break the dominance of Barcelona and Real Madrid.

He also earned a decent wage in a successful 19-year playing career, but has accumulated such a high net worth through management and an extensive property portfolio of over 180 apartments in Madrid that he oversees with his wife. Simeone became an ambassador for both Betinia and CampoBet in 2026 too.

Salah has utilised his amazing soccer career to amass huge wealth through lucrative contracts and a whole host of sponsorship deals. The Egyptian superstar became Liverpool’s highest-paid player ever in 2022, with a reported annual salary of £20m ($26.5m) in basic wages.

He has worked closely with major brands like Adidas, Pepsi, Vodafone and Uber, with estimates putting his endorsement income alone at around £15m per year ($19.8m) at its peak. Trabzonspor are paying the Premier League great around £15m ($19.8m) annually after he joined on a free transfer in the summer of 2026. His wider business interests are focused on real estate investment and commercial holding companies.

The first unusual name on this list comes in the form of ex-Chelsea and AC Milan striker Pato. He had a good career but failed to reach the lofty heights many expected of him, yet has turned that pain into power to become a hugely successful investor after his retirement. He did earn huge contracts at Milan and in a two-year stint in China, but his wealth mainly comes from off-field endeavours.

He has ventured into the world of gastronomy, with a chain of burger restaurants in Brasilia, while also putting his money into CoverGirl cosmetics, his own vodka brand and numerous properties in his home country. Pato is clearly looking to further his wealth in the future, after joining a consortium who completed a takeover of English club Northampton Town in 2026.

2026 Ballon d’Or winner Kane is not only loving life on the pitch with Bayern Munich and England, but he is also a supremely wealthy man off it, with a bank balance that stands head and shoulders above the rest of his international teammates. The Three Lions captain reportedly earns around £25m ($33.1m) each year before tax at Bayern Munich.

He boasts a high-profile commercial partnership with footwear brand Skechers, after signing a lifetime global deal in 2023 that earns him up to an estimated £7.5m ($9.9m) annually. Kane also regularly works with major brands like Allianz, Oura and Reflo.

The exceptional soccer career of Welsh superstar Bale translated into immense wealth, as he raked in over £500,000 per week ($661,625-a-week) in basic wages during the peak of his powers at Real Madrid. Commercial deals followed in abundance as he shone at the top of the game, with huge partnerships signed with Adidas, BMW, Lucozade and EA Sports.

Bale has dipped his toes into several different investment pathways since retiring, with a stake in a TGL golf franchise, co-ownership of a Cardiff-based bar and ties to Penderyn Whisky. His biggest step has undoubtedly been helping launch a sports investment fund worth over £500m ($661.6m), and Bale has also publicly admitted that he would like to co-own a soccer club in the near future.

Even soccer players on the level of Ronaldo were not paid close to the astronomical figures that relatively average players earn nowadays back in his time with some of the world’s biggest sides. He was one of the sport’s first truly global marketing superstars, though, signing a lifetime deal with Nike in 1994 and being one of the faces of their brand to this day.

Ronaldo boasts an endless list of partnerships with top brands that have all contributed to his huge fortune, with notable links to Santander, Betfair and Snickers. He actually had a bigger net worth in previous years, but failed investments at Spanish club Real Vallodolid and Brazilian side Cruzeiro have seen him fall down this list.

Mercurial genius Ibrahimovic has been able to transform his enigmatic persona as a player into a successful post-retirement career that has swelled his bank balance to new heights. He is one of the most recognisable soccer players of all time, and that is reflected in how unashamedly centred his commercial campaigns are on him.

After earning big money across his career with the likes of AC Milan, PSG, Barcelona and Man United, as well as being exceptionally well-paid by MLS standards at LA Galaxy, he has only continued to further his celebrity status through partnerships with Nike, Oakley Meta and XTB.

If you were waiting for the first mention of Saudi Arabian money impacting this list, then here it is. The oil-rich kingdom has enticed many of the world’s top names to the Middle East in the last five years with the promise of massive riches, and Benzema was no different. He joined Al Ittihad in 2023 and Al Hilal in 2026, with his latter contract reportedly worth over £1.6m each week ($2.1m) in basic wages.

Such incredible mega-deals came after a 14-year stay at Real Madrid that had already made him wealthy beyond comprehension. The 2022 Ballon d’Or winner maintained a long-standing relationship with Adidas until the contract expired when he was without a club in September 2026, while his effortless aura has also seen him link up with luxury brands like Fendi, Jean Paul Gaultier and Assaf.

Now a name that may only be familiar to British soccer fans, with Whelan being best known for his ownership of EFL side Wigan Athletic between 1995 and 2015. The Bradford native had a modest playing career but built his fortune after retirement by developing Whelan’s Discount Stores from the ground up and selling it on, then moving into sports retail with JJB Sports.

JJB grew exponentially in the UK as one of the market leaders for sportswear and equipment, and was valued at over £1bn ($1.32bn) at its peak in 2009. He then sold shares for a combined £240m ($317m) and effectively repeated the trick with DW Sports Fitness, all while pumping his money into Wigan to help them become 2013 FA Cup champions.

Rooney was consistently one of the highest-paid players in the world during his playing career. The Man United and England legend earned £300,000 per week ($396,975 per week) with his biggest contract extension in 2014, while he was one of the faces of Nike and synonymous with EA Sports’ FIFA franchise, appearing on seven consecutive covers between 2006 and 2012.

His status as one of the Premier League’s greatest ever players has seen the endless list of commercial opportunities continue post-retirement, with managerial deals, punditry contracts with the BBC and Sky, and his lucrative image-rights company keeping him afloat near the top of this list.

Mbappe has reached incredible heights over the last 10 years and is a global phenomenon who consistently ranks among the best scorers and players every season. Real Madrid pay him a reported £12.5m ($16.5m) in basic salary each year, while a £125m ($165.4m) signing-on bonus has been spread across his five-year deal. The French forward is not even in the prime of his career and has amassed a huge financial portfolio that rivals legends of the sport.

His commercial powerhouse has been accentuated by a massive Nike contract that ran for 20 years until its 2026 expiration, while major brands like Dior, Hublot and Oakley have all looked for a slice of the Mbappe pie with commercial endorsements in recent years.

You can be forgiven for potentially forgetting about the intricacies of Braithwaite’s soccer career, even though he has featured for the likes of Barcelona and Denmark. The Gremio forward’s huge fortune comes from a 2017 investment into American property developers NYCE Companies.

NYCE’s huge portfolio has expanded across the States in the last decade, with reports stating that they own and let out over 1,500 properties in several major cities. It was believed to have more than £270m ($357.3m) in assets in a 2026 report. Braithwaite has expanded his empire by investing into restaurants in Barcelona and Brazil, as well as establishing his own French fashion label.

Neymar still holds the world-record transfer fee from his eye-watering £200m ($263m) switch from Barcelona to Paris Saint-Germain in 2017. Paris is where the Brazilian superstar transformed from a generational prodigy into a commercial juggernaut, pocketing roughly £30m ($39m) a year in base wages before injury-hit spells and an eventual homecoming to boyhood club Santos.

His 2023 switch to Al Hilal saw utterly insane reported annual figures of £129m paid to the Selecao star as Saudi clubs looked to dislodge the European heavyweight leagues. He also reportedly signed a £23m yearly deal with Puma in 2020 after leaving Nike, while remaining in a lucrative partnership with Red Bull to this day.

David Beckham turned a lethal right foot and matinee-idol looks into the original athlete-as-a-global-brand blueprint. After winning everything on the pitch with Manchester United and Real Madrid, the Londoner became the ultimate pitchman—selling everything from underwear and fragrances to watches and whiskey for decades after hanging up his boots.

His shrewdest financial move came in 2007 when he signed for LA Galaxy, negotiating an expansion franchise option that allowed him to co-found Inter Miami for a fraction of its modern valuation. Combined with his Authentic Brands Group partnership and his Studio 99 production house, Brand Beckham has proven far more lucrative than his playing days ever were.

Being widely regarded as the greatest soccer player of all time still isn’t enough to crack the top four on this list—though Lionel Messi is hardly checking behind the sofa for spare change. Across legendary spells at Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain, and Inter Miami, the Argentine icon has cleared over £900m ($1.19bn) in career pre-tax playing earnings while securing a lucrative MLS equity pathway modeled on David Beckham’s playbook.

Off the pitch, Messi brings in a reported £56m ($74.1m) a year in 2026 through blockbuster partnerships with Adidas, Apple, Pepsi, and Konami. Eight Ballon d’Or trophies may not outrank royal oil money or biochemical startups here, but his commercial pull across the Americas remains unmatched.

In a fair world, spending 23 years at the summit of world soccer, becoming the sport’s first active billionaire, and collecting roughly $300m a year at Al Nassr would guarantee first place. Instead, Cristiano Ronaldo has to settle for fourth—making him easily the wealthiest player on this list who actually earned his fortune purely by kicking a ball.

The five-time Ballon d’Or winner became the first athlete to clear $2bn in career pre-tax earnings, boosted by a reported 15 percent equity stake in Al Nassr, a $1bn lifetime Nike contract signed in 2016, and his sprawling CR7 hotel and lifestyle empire. With more than 660 million Instagram followers, even a single sponsored post earns him more than most European pros make in a season.

During his playing days at Manchester United and Everton, Louis Saha was best known for clinical finishing and a frustratingly fragile hamstring. Since hanging up his boots, however, the former France striker has pulled off one of the greatest post-retirement glow-ups in sports history, building a tech fortune reportedly stretching into the multi-billions.

In 2014, Saha co-founded AxisStars, a private digital network that connects professional athletes and entertainers directly with vetted commercial partners and business ventures. Alongside savvy investments in AI and blockchain, Saha still pops up on television punditry panels—though at this point, he is clearly doing it for the love of the game rather than the appearance fee.

Arsenal fans remember Mathieu Flamini as a combative midfield enforcer famous for flying into two-footed tackles and cutting the sleeves off his matchday shirt. Few at the Emirates realized he was quietly building a green-energy empire between training sessions.

While studying law and still playing for the Gunners in 2013, Flamini co-founded GF Biochemicals, the first company to mass-produce levulinic acid as a sustainable alternative to petroleum. With estimates valuing his stake at up to £10bn ($13bn), the Frenchman is a regular fixture at global climate summits—and has refused to rule out buying a major soccer club of his own.

Faiq Bolkiah tops this list by £5bn ($6.6bn), proving once and for all that having the right uncle beats winning the Ballon d’Or. Born in Los Angeles, the winger spent time in the youth academies of Southampton, Chelsea, and Leicester City before playing senior club football in Portugal and Thailand—a modest resume that contrasts wildly with his status as soccer’s richest man.

Bolkiah is a member of the Brunei royal family and the nephew of Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, whose oil-and-gas fortune underpins an estimated £15bn ($19.85bn) family net worth. To his credit, Faiq has repeatedly played down his royal background so managers judge him on his football rather than his family vault.

#1922. Sources: Kevin de Bruyne’s most likely destination revealed amid Everton whispers

Transfer Correspondent AUTHORITY Former Sky Sports and ESPN FC correspondent who specialises in global recruitment, contract negotiations, and high-velocity transfer breaking news. FOCUS Exclusive reporting, domestic and international transfer markets, and elite-level insights. THE INSIGHT Pete utilises a Global Network of Industry Sources to deliver verified, first-to-market reporting. His “Deep-Lens” analysis connects the dots between boardroom strategy and pitch-level recruitment, providing a level of transfer clarity that goes beyond surface-level rumours.

Kevin De Bruyne is likelier to move to the MLS or the Saudi Pro League than return to the Premier League, sources have told Football Insider.

The 35-year-old has been linked with a move to Everton in recent days, with his contract at Napoli set to expire at the end of the season.

The Italian side have an option to extend it by an additional year but are yet to exercise the option, with the Belgian's future still uncertain.

As I revealed on the latest edition of Football Insider's Transfer Insider podcast, De Bruyne is unlikely to make the move to Everton if he does decide to leave.

The legendary midfielder left Manchester City in 2025, having won the Premier League six times and recorded nearly 300 direct goal involvements in an extremely successful 10 years.

De Bruyne struggled with injuries in his debut campaign with Napoli but looks to have returned to his best this season, scoring four goals and providing two assists in his first 15 appearances.

For the likes of Everton and the queue of other clubs who would dream of signing him, it is De Bruyne's wages which would be a sticking point in contract negotiations.

The midfielder reportedly took a pay cut to join Napoli, but he is still on a highly lucrative contract in Italy.

Speaking on the Transfer Insider podcast, I explained: "If De Bruyne was to leave Napoli any time soon, it's maybe more likely that he would go to a different league.

"Maybe the MLS could be something that would be of interest to him, and I would imagine there would be a lot of Saudi Pro League clubs who would love the opportunity to sign the Belgium international as well.

"So as things stand right now, I would say any move back to the Premier League is probably unlikely for De Bruyne."

While De Bruyne's move to Napoli appears to have been fuelled by his competitive spirit, he has previously admitted to being open to a move to the Saudi Pro League.

Speaking in 2024, he said: "At my age you have to be open to everything. You're talking about incredible amounts of money in what may be the end of my career.

"Sometimes you have to think about that. If I play there for two years, I will be able to earn an incredible amount of money. Before that I had to play football for 15 years. I may not even reach that amount yet.

"Then you have to think about what that could mean next. But at the moment I haven't had to think about that yet."

#1921. Luca Netz eyes Nottingham Forest revival as teammate's injury fears emerge - verdict

Correspondent AUTHORITY Sports journalist with experience at GamingINTEL and GRV Media; University of Wolverhampton graduate. FOCUS Data content, opinion, and general news coverage across the Breaking Media network. THE INSIGHT Scott utilises a network of club and industry contacts to deliver verified, broad-spectrum reporting. He provides the data and opinion foundations behind the headlines to ensure fans get the full story as it happens.

Luca Netz will be eyeing a Nottingham Forest revival, with a possible chance emerging following injury fears over Neco Williams.

The Forest defender was withdrawn early against Norway, with the Welshman seen limping heavily.

Williams has been a consistent and key performer for Forest, featuring in all 10 Premier League games, and only failing to play 90 minutes once across those.

Oliver Glasner will be sweating on the defender's fitness ahead of the return of domestic football.

Elsewhere in the squad, Netz has been rarely used by Glasner, and truthfully, since he arrived in the 2026 winter window.

But Netz may have to come into the side, as Williams' impressive display against Norway came to an end early.

Nottingham Forest will be hoping Williams is OK, but his heavy limping was not a great sign against Norway.

Williams, despite being 2-0 down to Norway, was having quite a good game against the Scandinavians.

The Nottingham Forest ace completed 91 per cent of his passing, and defensively had seven contributions as per FotMob.

These were made up of four tackles, two interceptions and one clearance, while he also managed to routinely come out on top in his duels.

He won 71 per cent of his ground duels (five out of seven) across his 72-minute performance.

This season, Williams has been used as a left-sided defender, and that is a position Forest do not have many natural options in.

It is safe to say that Netz hasn't exactly impressed Glasner at the City Ground, with the German left-back only making five appearances totalling 58 minutes.

The 23-year-old is clearly out of the manager's plans, but the latest with Williams could hand him a chance.

Of course, Forest are stacked in the wingback position, with Ola Aina also capable of filling in at left wingback.

But Netz is a natural left-footer, which certainly is an advantage for him.

While he also didn't feature much in 2025-26, there is at least enough data for his stats to emerge.

Netz ended the season in the 73rd percentile for expected assists per 90, and with more game time, perhaps he could have more influence.

Additionally, Netz' 0.11 xA per 90 is not too dissimilar to Williams' 0.12 from this season.

But, that will ultimately be up to Glasner to make a decision on.

#1920. ‘Looking back…’ – Alexander Isak speaks out over penalty controversy in defeat to Arsenal

Alexander Isak has spoken out about the controversial penalty incident in which he was involved during Liverpool’s defeat to Arsenal a fortnight ago.

Five minutes after Kai Havertz netted the only goal of the match, the Reds’ number 9 had his shirt pulled by Jurrien Timber inside the box, but neither on-field referee Andy Madley nor Stuart Attwell on VAR deemed it to have been a foul.

The transgression was unmistakably clear on replays, and the Premier League’s Key Match Incidents panel has since acknowledged that a spot kick should’ve been awarded.

Speaking to reporters whilst on international duty with Sweden, Isak was asked if he felt that he should’ve had a penalty.

He replied (Aftonbladet, via Liverpool Echo): “Yeah, looking back I suppose it does look that way, but when you’re in the moment, you don’t always perceive exactly what’s happening.

“I could feel myself being pulled a bit, but not to the extent that it appears later on. I was focused on scoring. It’s hard to try to score and then fall down at the same time. I was so locked in on the goal that I didn’t really register it.”

On whether he should’ve gone to ground to try and sway the referee, Isak said: “I don’t think there’s any need to embellish or go down on purpose. Sure, if I’d had a better read on the situation, I might have made sure the referee noticed it, that’s about all you can do, but I don’t believe you need to dive or exaggerate in situations like this.

“Perhaps it shouldn’t even matter that much, given that we have VAR and systems in place to make the decisive calls in these kinds of moments.”

Isak is absolutely right in saying that a penalty should’ve been awarded, and that he shouldn’t have to act unnaturally to convince the referee to give the decision in his team’s favour.

Andoni Iraola remarked after the game that a spot kick probably would’ve been given if the Liverpool striker had gone to ground, but the onus isn’t on players to sway the officials – it’s on the latter to get these big calls right, especially with recourse to VAR.

It feels as though the debate about officiating in the Premier League will continue indefinitely, with no discernible sign of an improvement in standards from Pro Ref figurehead Howard Webb.

It’s to Isak’s great credit that he’s given such a calm and measured verdict on the penalty incident when he and his team were so blatantly wronged. He’d have had every right to complain profusely about what happened; we’d suspect that many other players would’ve done so if they were in that situation.

He certainly hasn’t let it bother him in terms of his contributions on the pitch, with the 27-year-old scoring in Liverpool’s subsequent games against Fenerbahce and Crystal Palace to take his tally for the season to eight goals in 14 matches across all competitions.

That is, in fact, the best response to the injustice which was done against him Anfield two weeks ago.
